     28 ## About
     29 This is a minimal state immediate mode graphical user interface toolkit
     30 written in ANSI C and licensed under public domain. It was designed as a simple
     31 embeddable user interface for application and does not have any dependencies,
     32 a default renderbackend or OS window and input handling but instead provides a very modular
     33 library approach by using simple input state for input and draw
     34 commands describing primitive shapes as output. So instead of providing a
     35 layered library that tries to abstract over a number of platform and
     36 render backends it only focuses on the actual UI.
     37 
     38 ## Highlights
     39 - Graphical user interface toolkit
     40 - Single header library
     41 - Written in C89 (a.k.a. ANSI C or ISO C90)
     42 - Small codebase (~18kLOC)
     43 - Focus on portability, efficiency and simplicity
     44 - No dependencies (not even the standard library if not wanted)
     45 - Fully skinnable and customizable
     46 - Low memory footprint with total memory control if needed or wanted
     47 - UTF-8 support
     48 - No global or hidden state
     49 - Customizable library modules (you can compile and use only what you need)
     50 - Optional font baker and vertex buffer output
     51 - [Code available on github](https://github.com/Immediate-Mode-UI/Nuklear/)
     52 
     53 ## Features
     54 - Absolutely no platform dependent code
     55 - Memory management control ranging from/to
     56     - Ease of use by allocating everything from standard library
     57     - Control every byte of memory inside the library
     58 - Font handling control ranging from/to
     59     - Use your own font implementation for everything
     60     - Use this libraries internal font baking and handling API
     61 - Drawing output control ranging from/to
     62     - Simple shapes for more high level APIs which already have drawing capabilities
     63     - Hardware accessible anti-aliased vertex buffer output
     64 - Customizable colors and properties ranging from/to
     65     - Simple changes to color by filling a simple color table
     66     - Complete control with ability to use skinning to decorate widgets
     67 - Bendable UI library with widget ranging from/to
     68     - Basic widgets like buttons, checkboxes, slider, ...
     69     - Advanced widget like abstract comboboxes, contextual menus,...
     70 - Compile time configuration to only compile what you need
     71     - Subset which can be used if you do not want to link or use the standard library
     72 - Can be easily modified to only update on user input instead of frame updates
     73 
     74 ## Usage
     75 This library is self contained in one single header file and can be used either
     76 in header only mode or in implementation mode. The header only mode is used
     77 by default when included and allows including this header in other headers
     78 and does not contain the actual implementation. <br /><br />
     79 
     80 The implementation mode requires to define  the preprocessor macro
     81 NK_IMPLEMENTATION in *one* .c/.cpp file before #including this file, e.g.:
     82 
     83 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~C
     84     #define NK_IMPLEMENTATION
     85     #include "nuklear.h"
     86 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
     87 
     88 Also optionally define the symbols listed in the section "OPTIONAL DEFINES"
     89 below in header and implementation mode if you want to use additional functionality
     90 or need more control over the library.
     91 
     92 !!! WARNING
     93     Every time nuklear is included define the same compiler flags. This very important not doing so could lead to compiler errors or even worse stack corruptions.
     94 
     95 ### Flags
     96 Flag                            | Description
     97 --------------------------------|------------------------------------------
     98 NK_PRIVATE                      | If defined declares all functions as static, so they can only be accessed inside the file that contains the implementation
     99 NK_INCLUDE_FIXED_TYPES          | If defined it will include header `<stdint.h>` for fixed sized types otherwise nuklear tries to select the correct type. If that fails it will throw a compiler error and you have to select the correct types yourself.
    100 NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOCATOR    | If defined it will include header `<stdlib.h>` and provide additional functions to use this library without caring for memory allocation control and therefore ease memory management.
    101 NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_IO          | If defined it will include header `<stdio.h>` and provide additional functions depending on file loading.
    102 NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_VARARGS     | If defined it will include header <stdarg.h> and provide additional functions depending on file loading.
    103 NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_BOOL        | If defined it will include header `<stdbool.h>` for nk_bool otherwise nuklear defines nk_bool as int.
    104 NK_INCLUDE_VERTEX_BUFFER_OUTPUT | Defining this adds a vertex draw command list backend to this library, which allows you to convert queue commands into vertex draw commands. This is mainly if you need a hardware accessible format for OpenGL, DirectX, Vulkan, Metal,...
    105 NK_INCLUDE_FONT_BAKING          | Defining this adds `stb_truetype` and `stb_rect_pack` implementation to this library and provides font baking and rendering. If you already have font handling or do not want to use this font handler you don't have to define it.
    106 NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_FONT         | Defining this adds the default font: ProggyClean.ttf into this library which can be loaded into a font atlas and allows using this library without having a truetype font
    107 NK_INCLUDE_COMMAND_USERDATA     | Defining this adds a userdata pointer into each command. Can be useful for example if you want to provide custom shaders depending on the used widget. Can be combined with the style structures.
    108 NK_BUTTON_TRIGGER_ON_RELEASE    | Different platforms require button clicks occurring either on buttons being pressed (up to down) or released (down to up). By default this library will react on buttons being pressed, but if you define this it will only trigger if a button is released.
    109 NK_ZERO_COMMAND_MEMORY          | Defining this will zero out memory for each drawing command added to a drawing queue (inside nk_command_buffer_push). Zeroing command memory is very useful for fast checking (using memcmp) if command buffers are equal and avoid drawing frames when nothing on screen has changed since previous frame.
    110 NK_UINT_DRAW_INDEX              | Defining this will set the size of vertex index elements when using NK_VERTEX_BUFFER_OUTPUT to 32bit instead of the default of 16bit
    111 NK_KEYSTATE_BASED_INPUT         | Define this if your backend uses key state for each frame rather than key press/release events
    112 NK_IS_WORD_BOUNDARY(c)          | Define this to a function macro that takes a single nk_rune (nk_uint) and returns true if it's a word separator. If not defined, uses the default definition (see nk_is_word_boundary())
    113 
    114 !!! WARNING
    115     The following flags will pull in the standard C library:
    116     - NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOCATOR
    117     - NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_IO
    118     - NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_VARARGS
    119 
    120 !!! WARNING
    121     The following flags if defined need to be defined for both header and implementation:
    122     - NK_INCLUDE_FIXED_TYPES
    123     - NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOCATOR
    124     - NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_VARARGS
    125     - NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_BOOL
    126     - NK_INCLUDE_VERTEX_BUFFER_OUTPUT
    127     - NK_INCLUDE_FONT_BAKING
    128     - NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_FONT
    129     - NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_VARARGS
    130     - NK_INCLUDE_COMMAND_USERDATA
    131     - NK_UINT_DRAW_INDEX
    132 
    133 ### Constants
    134 Define                          | Description
    135 --------------------------------|---------------------------------------
    136 NK_BUFFER_DEFAULT_INITIAL_SIZE  | Initial buffer size allocated by all buffers while using the default allocator functions included by defining NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOCATOR. If you don't want to allocate the default 4k memory then redefine it.
    137 NK_MAX_NUMBER_BUFFER            | Maximum buffer size for the conversion buffer between float and string Under normal circumstances this should be more than sufficient.
    138 NK_INPUT_MAX                    | Defines the max number of bytes which can be added as text input in one frame. Under normal circumstances this should be more than sufficient.
    139 
    140 !!! WARNING
    141     The following constants if defined need to be defined for both header and implementation:
    142     - NK_MAX_NUMBER_BUFFER
    143     - NK_BUFFER_DEFAULT_INITIAL_SIZE
    144     - NK_INPUT_MAX
    145 
    146 ### Dependencies
    147 Function    | Description
    148 ------------|---------------------------------------------------------------
    149 NK_ASSERT   | If you don't define this, nuklear will use <assert.h> with assert().
    150 NK_MEMSET   | You can define this to 'memset' or your own memset implementation replacement. If not nuklear will use its own version.
    151 NK_MEMCPY   | You can define this to 'memcpy' or your own memcpy implementation replacement. If not nuklear will use its own version.
    152 NK_INV_SQRT | You can define this to your own inverse sqrt implementation replacement. If not nuklear will use its own slow and not highly accurate version.
    153 NK_SIN      | You can define this to 'sinf' or your own sine implementation replacement. If not nuklear will use its own approximation implementation.
    154 NK_COS      | You can define this to 'cosf' or your own cosine implementation replacement. If not nuklear will use its own approximation implementation.
    155 NK_STRTOD   | You can define this to `strtod` or your own string to double conversion implementation replacement. If not defined nuklear will use its own imprecise and possibly unsafe version (does not handle nan or infinity!).
    156 NK_DTOA     | You can define this to `dtoa` or your own double to string conversion implementation replacement. If not defined nuklear will use its own imprecise and possibly unsafe version (does not handle nan or infinity!).
    157 NK_VSNPRINTF| If you define `NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_VARARGS` as well as `NK_INCLUDE_STANDARD_IO` and want to be safe define this to `vsnprintf` on compilers supporting later versions of C or C++. By default nuklear will check for your stdlib version in C as well as compiler version in C++. if `vsnprintf` is available it will define it to `vsnprintf` directly. If not defined and if you have older versions of C or C++ it will be defined to `vsprintf` which is unsafe.
    158 
    159 !!! WARNING
    160     The following dependencies will pull in the standard C library if not redefined:
    161     - NK_ASSERT
    162 
    163 !!! WARNING
    164     The following dependencies if defined need to be defined for both header and implementation:
    165     - NK_ASSERT
    166 
    167 !!! WARNING
    168     The following dependencies if defined need to be defined only for the implementation part:
    169     - NK_MEMSET
    170     - NK_MEMCPY
    171     - NK_SQRT
    172     - NK_SIN
    173     - NK_COS
    174     - NK_STRTOD
    175     - NK_DTOA
    176     - NK_VSNPRINTF

    178 ## Example
    179 
    180 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~c
    181 // init gui state
    182 enum {EASY, HARD};
    183 static int op = EASY;
    184 static float value = 0.6f;
    185 static int i =  20;
    186 struct nk_context ctx;
    187 
    188 nk_init_fixed(&ctx, calloc(1, MAX_MEMORY), MAX_MEMORY, &font);
    189 if (nk_begin(&ctx, "Show", nk_rect(50, 50, 220, 220),
    190     NK_WINDOW_BORDER|NK_WINDOW_MOVABLE|NK_WINDOW_CLOSABLE)) {
    191     // fixed widget pixel width
    192     nk_layout_row_static(&ctx, 30, 80, 1);
    193     if (nk_button_label(&ctx, "button")) {
    194         // event handling
    195     }
    196 
    197     // fixed widget window ratio width
    198     nk_layout_row_dynamic(&ctx, 30, 2);
    199     if (nk_option_label(&ctx, "easy", op == EASY)) op = EASY;
    200     if (nk_option_label(&ctx, "hard", op == HARD)) op = HARD;
    201 
    202     // custom widget pixel width
    203     nk_layout_row_begin(&ctx, NK_STATIC, 30, 2);
    204     {
    205         nk_layout_row_push(&ctx, 50);
    206         nk_label(&ctx, "Volume:", NK_TEXT_LEFT);
    207         nk_layout_row_push(&ctx, 110);
    208         nk_slider_float(&ctx, 0, &value, 1.0f, 0.1f);
    209     }
    210     nk_layout_row_end(&ctx);
    211 }
    212 nk_end(&ctx);
    213 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

    534     NK_SYMBOL_MINUS,
    535     NK_SYMBOL_TRIANGLE_UP_OUTLINE,
    536     NK_SYMBOL_TRIANGLE_DOWN_OUTLINE,
    537     NK_SYMBOL_TRIANGLE_LEFT_OUTLINE,
    538     NK_SYMBOL_TRIANGLE_RIGHT_OUTLINE,
    539     NK_SYMBOL_MAX
    540 };
    541 /* =============================================================================
    542  *
    543  *                                  CONTEXT
    544  *
    545  * =============================================================================*/
    546 /**
    547  * \page Context
    548  * Contexts are the main entry point and the majestro of nuklear and contain all required state.
    549  * They are used for window, memory, input, style, stack, commands and time management and need
    550  * to be passed into all nuklear GUI specific functions.
    551  *
    552  * # Usage
    553  * To use a context it first has to be initialized which can be achieved by calling
    554  * one of either `nk_init_default`, `nk_init_fixed`, `nk_init`, `nk_init_custom`.
    555  * Each takes in a font handle and a specific way of handling memory. Memory control
    556  * hereby ranges from standard library to just specifying a fixed sized block of memory
    557  * which nuklear has to manage itself from.
    558  *
    559  * ```c
    560  * struct nk_context ctx;
    561  * nk_init_xxx(&ctx, ...);
    562  * while (1) {
    563  *     // [...]
    564  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
    565  * }
    566  * nk_free(&ctx);
    567  * ```
    568  *
    569  * # Reference
    570  * Function            | Description
    571  * --------------------|-------------------------------------------------------
    572  * \ref nk_init_default | Initializes context with standard library memory allocation (malloc,free)
    573  * \ref nk_init_fixed   | Initializes context from single fixed size memory block
    574  * \ref nk_init         | Initializes context with memory allocator callbacks for alloc and free
    575  * \ref nk_init_custom  | Initializes context from two buffers. One for draw commands the other for window/panel/table allocations
    576  * \ref nk_clear        | Called at the end of the frame to reset and prepare the context for the next frame
    577  * \ref nk_free         | Shutdown and free all memory allocated inside the context
    578  * \ref nk_set_user_data| Utility function to pass user data to draw command
    579  */
    580 
    581 #ifdef NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOCATOR
    582 
    583 /**
    584  * # nk_init_default
    585  * Initializes a `nk_context` struct with a default standard library allocator.
    586  * Should be used if you don't want to be bothered with memory management in nuklear.
    587  *
    588  * ```c
    589  * nk_bool nk_init_default(struct nk_context *ctx, const struct nk_user_font *font);
    590  * ```
    591  *
    592  * Parameter   | Description
    593  * ------------|---------------------------------------------------------------
    594  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an either stack or heap allocated `nk_context` struct
    595  * \param[in] font    | Must point to a previously initialized font handle for more info look at font documentation
    596  *
    597  * \returns either `false(0)` on failure or `true(1)` on success.
    598  */
    599 NK_API nk_bool nk_init_default(struct nk_context*, const struct nk_user_font*);
    600 #endif
    601 /**
    602  * # nk_init_fixed
    603  * Initializes a `nk_context` struct from single fixed size memory block
    604  * Should be used if you want complete control over nuklear's memory management.
    605  * Especially recommended for system with little memory or systems with virtual memory.
    606  * For the later case you can just allocate for example 16MB of virtual memory
    607  * and only the required amount of memory will actually be committed.
    608  *
    609  * ```c
    610  * nk_bool nk_init_fixed(struct nk_context *ctx, void *memory, nk_size size, const struct nk_user_font *font);
    611  * ```
    612  *
    613  * !!! Warning
    614  *     make sure the passed memory block is aligned correctly for `nk_draw_commands`.
    615  *
    616  * Parameter   | Description
    617  * ------------|--------------------------------------------------------------
    618  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an either stack or heap allocated `nk_context` struct
    619  * \param[in] memory  | Must point to a previously allocated memory block
    620  * \param[in] size    | Must contain the total size of memory
    621  * \param[in] font    | Must point to a previously initialized font handle for more info look at font documentation
    622  *
    623  * \returns either `false(0)` on failure or `true(1)` on success.
    624  */
    625 NK_API nk_bool nk_init_fixed(struct nk_context*, void *memory, nk_size size, const struct nk_user_font*);
    626 
    627 /**
    628  * # nk_init
    629  * Initializes a `nk_context` struct with memory allocation callbacks for nuklear to allocate
    630  * memory from. Used internally for `nk_init_default` and provides a kitchen sink allocation
    631  * interface to nuklear. Can be useful for cases like monitoring memory consumption.
    632  *
    633  * ```c
    634  * nk_bool nk_init(struct nk_context *ctx, const struct nk_allocator *alloc, const struct nk_user_font *font);
    635  * ```
    636  *
    637  * Parameter   | Description
    638  * ------------|---------------------------------------------------------------
    639  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an either stack or heap allocated `nk_context` struct
    640  * \param[in] alloc   | Must point to a previously allocated memory allocator
    641  * \param[in] font    | Must point to a previously initialized font handle for more info look at font documentation
    642  *
    643  * \returns either `false(0)` on failure or `true(1)` on success.
    644  */
    645 NK_API nk_bool nk_init(struct nk_context*, const struct nk_allocator*, const struct nk_user_font*);
    646 
    647 /**
    648  * \brief Initializes a `nk_context` struct from two different either fixed or growing buffers.
    649  *
    650  * \details
    651  * The first buffer is for allocating draw commands while the second buffer is
    652  * used for allocating windows, panels and state tables.
    653  *
    654  * ```c
    655  * nk_bool nk_init_custom(struct nk_context *ctx, struct nk_buffer *cmds, struct nk_buffer *pool, const struct nk_user_font *font);
    656  * ```
    657  *
    658  * \param[in] ctx    Must point to an either stack or heap allocated `nk_context` struct
    659  * \param[in] cmds   Must point to a previously initialized memory buffer either fixed or dynamic to store draw commands into
    660  * \param[in] pool   Must point to a previously initialized memory buffer either fixed or dynamic to store windows, panels and tables
    661  * \param[in] font   Must point to a previously initialized font handle for more info look at font documentation
    662  *
    663  * \returns either `false(0)` on failure or `true(1)` on success.
    664  */
    665 NK_API nk_bool nk_init_custom(struct nk_context*, struct nk_buffer *cmds, struct nk_buffer *pool, const struct nk_user_font*);
    666 
    667 /**
    668  * \brief Resets the context state at the end of the frame.
    669  *
    670  * \details
    671  * This includes mostly garbage collector tasks like removing windows or table
    672  * not called and therefore used anymore.
    673  *
    674  * ```c
    675  * void nk_clear(struct nk_context *ctx);
    676  * ```
    677  *
    678  * \param[in] ctx  Must point to a previously initialized `nk_context` struct
    679  */
    680 NK_API void nk_clear(struct nk_context*);
    681 
    682 /**
    683  * \brief Frees all memory allocated by nuklear; Not needed if context was initialized with `nk_init_fixed`.
    684  *
    685  * \details
    686  * ```c
    687  * void nk_free(struct nk_context *ctx);
    688  * ```
    689  *
    690  * \param[in] ctx  Must point to a previously initialized `nk_context` struct
    691  */
    692 NK_API void nk_free(struct nk_context*);
    693 
    694 #ifdef NK_INCLUDE_COMMAND_USERDATA
    695 /**
    696  * \brief Sets the currently passed userdata passed down into each draw command.
    697  *
    698  * \details
    699  * ```c
    700  * void nk_set_user_data(struct nk_context *ctx, nk_handle data);
    701  * ```
    702  *
    703  * \param[in] ctx Must point to a previously initialized `nk_context` struct
    704  * \param[in] data  Handle with either pointer or index to be passed into every draw commands
    705  */
    706 NK_API void nk_set_user_data(struct nk_context*, nk_handle handle);
    707 #endif
    708 /* =============================================================================
    709  *
    710  *                                  INPUT
    711  *
    712  * =============================================================================*/
    713 /**
    714  * \page Input
    715  *
    716  * The input API is responsible for holding the current input state composed of
    717  * mouse, key and text input states.
    718  * It is worth noting that no direct OS or window handling is done in nuklear.
    719  * Instead all input state has to be provided by platform specific code. This on one hand
    720  * expects more work from the user and complicates usage but on the other hand
    721  * provides simple abstraction over a big number of platforms, libraries and other
    722  * already provided functionality.
    723  *
    724  * ```c
    725  * nk_input_begin(&ctx);
    726  * while (GetEvent(&evt)) {
    727  *     if (evt.type == MOUSE_MOVE)
    728  *         nk_input_motion(&ctx, evt.motion.x, evt.motion.y);
    729  *     else if (evt.type == [...]) {
    730  *         // [...]
    731  *     }
    732  * } nk_input_end(&ctx);
    733  * ```
    734  *
    735  * # Usage
    736  * Input state needs to be provided to nuklear by first calling `nk_input_begin`
    737  * which resets internal state like delta mouse position and button transitions.
    738  * After `nk_input_begin` all current input state needs to be provided. This includes
    739  * mouse motion, button and key pressed and released, text input and scrolling.
    740  * Both event- or state-based input handling are supported by this API
    741  * and should work without problems. Finally after all input state has been
    742  * mirrored `nk_input_end` needs to be called to finish input process.
    743  *
    744  * ```c
    745  * struct nk_context ctx;
    746  * nk_init_xxx(&ctx, ...);
    747  * while (1) {
    748  *     Event evt;
    749  *     nk_input_begin(&ctx);
    750  *     while (GetEvent(&evt)) {
    751  *         if (evt.type == MOUSE_MOVE)
    752  *             nk_input_motion(&ctx, evt.motion.x, evt.motion.y);
    753  *         else if (evt.type == [...]) {
    754  *             // [...]
    755  *         }
    756  *     }
    757  *     nk_input_end(&ctx);
    758  *     // [...]
    759  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
    760  * } nk_free(&ctx);
    761  * ```
    762  *
    763  * # Reference
    764  * Function            | Description
    765  * --------------------|-------------------------------------------------------
    766  * \ref nk_input_begin  | Begins the input mirroring process. Needs to be called before all other `nk_input_xxx` calls
    767  * \ref nk_input_motion | Mirrors mouse cursor position
    768  * \ref nk_input_key    | Mirrors key state with either pressed or released
    769  * \ref nk_input_button | Mirrors mouse button state with either pressed or released
    770  * \ref nk_input_scroll | Mirrors mouse scroll values
    771  * \ref nk_input_char   | Adds a single ASCII text character into an internal text buffer
    772  * \ref nk_input_glyph  | Adds a single multi-byte UTF-8 character into an internal text buffer
    773  * \ref nk_input_unicode| Adds a single unicode rune into an internal text buffer
    774  * \ref nk_input_end    | Ends the input mirroring process by calculating state changes. Don't call any `nk_input_xxx` function referenced above after this call
    775  */
    776 
    777 enum nk_keys {
    778     NK_KEY_NONE,
    779     NK_KEY_SHIFT,
    780     NK_KEY_CTRL,
    781     NK_KEY_DEL,
    782     NK_KEY_ENTER,
    783     NK_KEY_TAB,
    784     NK_KEY_BACKSPACE,
    785     NK_KEY_COPY,
    786     NK_KEY_CUT,
    787     NK_KEY_PASTE,
    788     NK_KEY_UP,
    789     NK_KEY_DOWN,
    790     NK_KEY_LEFT,
    791     NK_KEY_RIGHT,
    792     /* Shortcuts: text field */
    793     NK_KEY_TEXT_INSERT_MODE,
    794     NK_KEY_TEXT_REPLACE_MODE,
    795     NK_KEY_TEXT_RESET_MODE,
    796     NK_KEY_TEXT_LINE_START,
    797     NK_KEY_TEXT_LINE_END,
    798     NK_KEY_TEXT_START,
    799     NK_KEY_TEXT_END,
    800     NK_KEY_TEXT_UNDO,
    801     NK_KEY_TEXT_REDO,
    802     NK_KEY_TEXT_SELECT_ALL,
    803     NK_KEY_TEXT_WORD_LEFT,
    804     NK_KEY_TEXT_WORD_RIGHT,
    805     /* Shortcuts: scrollbar */
    806     NK_KEY_SCROLL_START,
    807     NK_KEY_SCROLL_END,
    808     NK_KEY_SCROLL_DOWN,
    809     NK_KEY_SCROLL_UP,
    810     NK_KEY_MAX
    811 };
    812 enum nk_buttons {
    813     NK_BUTTON_LEFT,
    814     NK_BUTTON_MIDDLE,
    815     NK_BUTTON_RIGHT,
    816     NK_BUTTON_DOUBLE,
    817     NK_BUTTON_MAX
    818 };

    820 /**
    821  * \brief Begins the input mirroring process by resetting text, scroll
    822  * mouse, previous mouse position and movement as well as key state transitions.
    823  *
    824  * \details
    825  * ```c
    826  * void nk_input_begin(struct nk_context*);
    827  * ```
    828  *
    829  * \param[in] ctx Must point to a previously initialized `nk_context` struct
    830  */
    831 NK_API void nk_input_begin(struct nk_context*);
    832 
    833 /**
    834  * \brief Mirrors current mouse position to nuklear
    835  *
    836  * \details
    837  * ```c
    838  * void nk_input_motion(struct nk_context *ctx, int x, int y);
    839  * ```
    840  *
    841  * \param[in] ctx   Must point to a previously initialized `nk_context` struct
    842  * \param[in] x     Must hold an integer describing the current mouse cursor x-position
    843  * \param[in] y     Must hold an integer describing the current mouse cursor y-position
    844  */
    845 NK_API void nk_input_motion(struct nk_context*, int x, int y);

    847 /**

    849  *

    852  * void nk_input_key(struct nk_context*, enum nk_keys key, nk_bool down);
    853  * ```

    867  * ```
    868  *
    869  * \param[in] ctx     Must point to a previously initialized `nk_context` struct

    872  * \param[in] y       Must contain an integer describing mouse cursor y-position on click up/down

    893 /**
    894  * \brief Copies a single ASCII character into an internal text buffer

    897  * This is basically a helper function to quickly push ASCII characters into

    901  *     Stores up to NK_INPUT_MAX bytes between `nk_input_begin` and `nk_input_end`.

    903  * ```c

    945 /**
    946  * \brief End the input mirroring process by resetting mouse grabbing
    947  * state to ensure the mouse cursor is not grabbed indefinitely.

    949  * \details

    951  * void nk_input_end(struct nk_context *ctx);

    958 /** =============================================================================
    959  *
    960  *                                  DRAWING
    961  *
    962  * =============================================================================*/
    963 /**
    964  * \page Drawing
    965  * This library was designed to be render backend agnostic so it does
    966  * not draw anything to screen directly. Instead all drawn shapes, widgets
    967  * are made of, are buffered into memory and make up a command queue.
    968  * Each frame therefore fills the command buffer with draw commands
    969  * that then need to be executed by the user and his own render backend.
    970  * After that the command buffer needs to be cleared and a new frame can be
    971  * started. It is probably important to note that the command buffer is the main
    972  * drawing API and the optional vertex buffer API only takes this format and
    973  * converts it into a hardware accessible format.
    974  *
    975  * # Usage
    976  * To draw all draw commands accumulated over a frame you need your own render
    977  * backend able to draw a number of 2D primitives. This includes at least
    978  * filled and stroked rectangles, circles, text, lines, triangles and scissors.
    979  * As soon as this criterion is met you can iterate over each draw command
    980  * and execute each draw command in a interpreter like fashion:
    981  *
    982  * ```c
    983  * const struct nk_command *cmd = 0;
    984  * nk_foreach(cmd, &ctx) {
    985  *     switch (cmd->type) {
    986  *     case NK_COMMAND_LINE:
    987  *         your_draw_line_function(...)
    988  *         break;
    989  *     case NK_COMMAND_RECT
    990  *         your_draw_rect_function(...)
    991  *         break;
    992  *     case //...:
    993  *         //[...]
    994  *     }
    995  * }
    996  * ```
    997  *
    998  * In program flow context draw commands need to be executed after input has been
    999  * gathered and the complete UI with windows and their contained widgets have
   1000  * been executed and before calling `nk_clear` which frees all previously
   1001  * allocated draw commands.
   1002  *
   1003  * ```c
   1004  * struct nk_context ctx;
   1005  * nk_init_xxx(&ctx, ...);
   1006  * while (1) {
   1007  *     Event evt;
   1008  *     nk_input_begin(&ctx);
   1009  *     while (GetEvent(&evt)) {
   1010  *         if (evt.type == MOUSE_MOVE)
   1011  *             nk_input_motion(&ctx, evt.motion.x, evt.motion.y);
   1012  *         else if (evt.type == [...]) {
   1013  *             [...]
   1014  *         }
   1015  *     }
   1016  *     nk_input_end(&ctx);
   1017  *     //
   1018  *     // [...]
   1019  *     //
   1020  *     const struct nk_command *cmd = 0;
   1021  *     nk_foreach(cmd, &ctx) {
   1022  *     switch (cmd->type) {
   1023  *     case NK_COMMAND_LINE:
   1024  *         your_draw_line_function(...)
   1025  *         break;
   1026  *     case NK_COMMAND_RECT
   1027  *         your_draw_rect_function(...)
   1028  *         break;
   1029  *     case ...:
   1030  *         // [...]
   1031  *     }
   1032  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
   1033  * }
   1034  * nk_free(&ctx);
   1035  * ```
   1036  *
   1037  * You probably noticed that you have to draw all of the UI each frame which is
   1038  * quite wasteful. While the actual UI updating loop is quite fast rendering
   1039  * without actually needing it is not. So there are multiple things you could do.
   1040  *
   1041  * First is only update on input. This of course is only an option if your
   1042  * application only depends on the UI and does not require any outside calculations.
   1043  * If you actually only update on input make sure to update the UI two times each
   1044  * frame and call `nk_clear` directly after the first pass and only draw in
   1045  * the second pass. In addition it is recommended to also add additional timers
   1046  * to make sure the UI is not drawn more than a fixed number of frames per second.
   1047  *
   1048  * ```c
   1049  * struct nk_context ctx;
   1050  * nk_init_xxx(&ctx, ...);
   1051  * while (1) {
   1052  *     // [...wait for input ]
   1053  *     // [...do two UI passes ...]
   1054  *     do_ui(...)
   1055  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
   1056  *     do_ui(...)
   1057  *     //
   1058  *     // draw
   1059  *     const struct nk_command *cmd = 0;
   1060  *     nk_foreach(cmd, &ctx) {
   1061  *     switch (cmd->type) {
   1062  *     case NK_COMMAND_LINE:
   1063  *         your_draw_line_function(...)
   1064  *         break;
   1065  *     case NK_COMMAND_RECT
   1066  *         your_draw_rect_function(...)
   1067  *         break;
   1068  *     case ...:
   1069  *         //[...]
   1070  *     }
   1071  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
   1072  * }
   1073  * nk_free(&ctx);
   1074  * ```
   1075  *
   1076  * The second probably more applicable trick is to only draw if anything changed.
   1077  * It is not really useful for applications with continuous draw loop but
   1078  * quite useful for desktop applications. To actually get nuklear to only
   1079  * draw on changes you first have to define `NK_ZERO_COMMAND_MEMORY` and
   1080  * allocate a memory buffer that will store each unique drawing output.
   1081  * After each frame you compare the draw command memory inside the library
   1082  * with your allocated buffer by memcmp. If memcmp detects differences
   1083  * you have to copy the command buffer into the allocated buffer
   1084  * and then draw like usual (this example uses fixed memory but you could
   1085  * use dynamically allocated memory).
   1086  *
   1087  * ```c
   1088  * //[... other defines ...]
   1089  * #define NK_ZERO_COMMAND_MEMORY
   1090  * #include "nuklear.h"
   1091  * //
   1092  * // setup context
   1093  * struct nk_context ctx;
   1094  * void *last = calloc(1,64*1024);
   1095  * void *buf = calloc(1,64*1024);
   1096  * nk_init_fixed(&ctx, buf, 64*1024);
   1097  * //
   1098  * // loop
   1099  * while (1) {
   1100  *     // [...input...]
   1101  *     // [...ui...]
   1102  *     void *cmds = nk_buffer_memory(&ctx.memory);
   1103  *     if (memcmp(cmds, last, ctx.memory.allocated)) {
   1104  *         memcpy(last,cmds,ctx.memory.allocated);
   1105  *         const struct nk_command *cmd = 0;
   1106  *         nk_foreach(cmd, &ctx) {
   1107  *             switch (cmd->type) {
   1108  *             case NK_COMMAND_LINE:
   1109  *                 your_draw_line_function(...)
   1110  *                 break;
   1111  *             case NK_COMMAND_RECT
   1112  *                 your_draw_rect_function(...)
   1113  *                 break;
   1114  *             case ...:
   1115  *                 // [...]
   1116  *             }
   1117  *         }
   1118  *     }
   1119  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
   1120  * }
   1121  * nk_free(&ctx);
   1122  * ```
   1123  *
   1124  * Finally while using draw commands makes sense for higher abstracted platforms like
   1125  * X11 and Win32 or drawing libraries it is often desirable to use graphics
   1126  * hardware directly. Therefore it is possible to just define
   1127  * `NK_INCLUDE_VERTEX_BUFFER_OUTPUT` which includes optional vertex output.
   1128  * To access the vertex output you first have to convert all draw commands into
   1129  * vertexes by calling `nk_convert` which takes in your preferred vertex format.
   1130  * After successfully converting all draw commands just iterate over and execute all
   1131  * vertex draw commands:
   1132  *
   1133  * ```c
   1134  * // fill configuration
   1135  * struct your_vertex
   1136  * {
   1137  *     float pos[2]; // important to keep it to 2 floats
   1138  *     float uv[2];
   1139  *     unsigned char col[4];
   1140  * };
   1141  * struct nk_convert_config cfg = {};
   1142  * static const struct nk_draw_vertex_layout_element vertex_layout[] = {
   1143  *     {NK_VERTEX_POSITION, NK_FORMAT_FLOAT, NK_OFFSETOF(struct your_vertex, pos)},
   1144  *     {NK_VERTEX_TEXCOORD, NK_FORMAT_FLOAT, NK_OFFSETOF(struct your_vertex, uv)},
   1145  *     {NK_VERTEX_COLOR, NK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8, NK_OFFSETOF(struct your_vertex, col)},
   1146  *     {NK_VERTEX_LAYOUT_END}
   1147  * };
   1148  * cfg.shape_AA = NK_ANTI_ALIASING_ON;
   1149  * cfg.line_AA = NK_ANTI_ALIASING_ON;
   1150  * cfg.vertex_layout = vertex_layout;
   1151  * cfg.vertex_size = sizeof(struct your_vertex);
   1152  * cfg.vertex_alignment = NK_ALIGNOF(struct your_vertex);
   1153  * cfg.circle_segment_count = 22;
   1154  * cfg.curve_segment_count = 22;
   1155  * cfg.arc_segment_count = 22;
   1156  * cfg.global_alpha = 1.0f;
   1157  * cfg.tex_null = dev->tex_null;
   1158  * //
   1159  * // setup buffers and convert
   1160  * struct nk_buffer cmds, verts, idx;
   1161  * nk_buffer_init_default(&cmds);
   1162  * nk_buffer_init_default(&verts);
   1163  * nk_buffer_init_default(&idx);
   1164  * nk_convert(&ctx, &cmds, &verts, &idx, &cfg);
   1165  * //
   1166  * // draw
   1167  * nk_draw_foreach(cmd, &ctx, &cmds) {
   1168  * if (!cmd->elem_count) continue;
   1169  *     //[...]
   1170  * }
   1171  * nk_buffer_free(&cms);
   1172  * nk_buffer_free(&verts);
   1173  * nk_buffer_free(&idx);
   1174  * ```
   1175  *
   1176  * # Reference
   1177  * Function            | Description
   1178  * --------------------|-------------------------------------------------------
   1179  * \ref nk__begin       | Returns the first draw command in the context draw command list to be drawn
   1180  * \ref nk__next        | Increments the draw command iterator to the next command inside the context draw command list
   1181  * \ref nk_foreach      | Iterates over each draw command inside the context draw command list
   1182  * \ref nk_convert      | Converts from the abstract draw commands list into a hardware accessible vertex format
   1183  * \ref nk_draw_begin   | Returns the first vertex command in the context vertex draw list to be executed
   1184  * \ref nk__draw_next   | Increments the vertex command iterator to the next command inside the context vertex command list
   1185  * \ref nk__draw_end    | Returns the end of the vertex draw list
   1186  * \ref nk_draw_foreach | Iterates over each vertex draw command inside the vertex draw list
   1187  */
   1188 
   1189 enum nk_anti_aliasing {NK_ANTI_ALIASING_OFF, NK_ANTI_ALIASING_ON};
   1190 enum nk_convert_result {
   1191     NK_CONVERT_SUCCESS = 0,
   1192     NK_CONVERT_INVALID_PARAM = 1,
   1193     NK_CONVERT_COMMAND_BUFFER_FULL = NK_FLAG(1),
   1194     NK_CONVERT_VERTEX_BUFFER_FULL = NK_FLAG(2),
   1195     NK_CONVERT_ELEMENT_BUFFER_FULL = NK_FLAG(3)
   1196 };
   1197 struct nk_draw_null_texture {
   1198     nk_handle texture; /**!< texture handle to a texture with a white pixel */
   1199     struct nk_vec2 uv; /**!< coordinates to a white pixel in the texture  */
   1200 };
   1201 struct nk_convert_config {
   1202     float global_alpha;             /**!< global alpha value */
   1203     enum nk_anti_aliasing line_AA;  /**!< line anti-aliasing flag can be turned off if you are tight on memory */
   1204     enum nk_anti_aliasing shape_AA; /**!< shape anti-aliasing flag can be turned off if you are tight on memory */
   1205     unsigned circle_segment_count;  /**!< number of segments used for circles: default to 22 */
   1206     unsigned arc_segment_count;     /**!< number of segments used for arcs: default to 22 */
   1207     unsigned curve_segment_count;   /**!< number of segments used for curves: default to 22 */
   1208     struct nk_draw_null_texture tex_null; /**!< handle to texture with a white pixel for shape drawing */
   1209     const struct nk_draw_vertex_layout_element *vertex_layout; /**!< describes the vertex output format and packing */
   1210     nk_size vertex_size;      /**!< sizeof one vertex for vertex packing */
   1211     nk_size vertex_alignment; /**!< vertex alignment: Can be obtained by NK_ALIGNOF */
   1212 };
   1213 
   1214 /**
   1215  * \brief Returns a draw command list iterator to iterate all draw
   1216  * commands accumulated over one frame.
   1217  *
   1218  * \details
   1219  * ```c
   1220  * const struct nk_command* nk__begin(struct nk_context*);
   1221  * ```
   1222  *
   1223  * \param[in] ctx     | must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1224  *
   1225  * \returns draw command pointer pointing to the first command inside the draw command list
   1226  */
   1227 NK_API const struct nk_command* nk__begin(struct nk_context*);
   1228 
   1229 /**
   1230  * \brief Returns draw command pointer pointing to the next command inside the draw command list
   1231  *
   1232  * \details
   1233  * ```c
   1234  * const struct nk_command* nk__next(struct nk_context*, const struct nk_command*);
   1235  * ```
   1236  *
   1237  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1238  * \param[in] cmd     | Must point to an previously a draw command either returned by `nk__begin` or `nk__next`
   1239  *
   1240  * \returns draw command pointer pointing to the next command inside the draw command list
   1241  */
   1242 NK_API const struct nk_command* nk__next(struct nk_context*, const struct nk_command*);
   1243 
   1244 /**
   1245  * \brief Iterates over each draw command inside the context draw command list
   1246  *
   1247  * ```c
   1248  * #define nk_foreach(c, ctx)
   1249  * ```
   1250  *
   1251  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1252  * \param[in] cmd     | Command pointer initialized to NULL
   1253  */
   1254 #define nk_foreach(c, ctx) for((c) = nk__begin(ctx); (c) != 0; (c) = nk__next(ctx,c))
   1255 
   1256 #ifdef NK_INCLUDE_VERTEX_BUFFER_OUTPUT
   1257 
   1258 /**
   1259  * \brief Converts all internal draw commands into vertex draw commands and fills
   1260  * three buffers with vertexes, vertex draw commands and vertex indices.
   1261  *
   1262  * \details
   1263  * The vertex format as well as some other configuration values have to be
   1264  * configured by filling out a `nk_convert_config` struct.
   1265  *
   1266  * ```c
   1267  * nk_flags nk_convert(struct nk_context *ctx, struct nk_buffer *cmds,
   1268  *     struct nk_buffer *vertices, struct nk_buffer *elements, const struct nk_convert_config*);
   1269  * ```
   1270  *
   1271  * \param[in] ctx      Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1272  * \param[out] cmds     Must point to a previously initialized buffer to hold converted vertex draw commands
   1273  * \param[out] vertices Must point to a previously initialized buffer to hold all produced vertices
   1274  * \param[out] elements Must point to a previously initialized buffer to hold all produced vertex indices
   1275  * \param[in] config   Must point to a filled out `nk_config` struct to configure the conversion process
   1276  *
   1277  * \returns one of enum nk_convert_result error codes
   1278  *
   1279  * Parameter                       | Description
   1280  * --------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   1281  * NK_CONVERT_SUCCESS              | Signals a successful draw command to vertex buffer conversion
   1282  * NK_CONVERT_INVALID_PARAM        | An invalid argument was passed in the function call
   1283  * NK_CONVERT_COMMAND_BUFFER_FULL  | The provided buffer for storing draw commands is full or failed to allocate more memory
   1284  * NK_CONVERT_VERTEX_BUFFER_FULL   | The provided buffer for storing vertices is full or failed to allocate more memory
   1285  * NK_CONVERT_ELEMENT_BUFFER_FULL  | The provided buffer for storing indices is full or failed to allocate more memory
   1286  */
   1287 NK_API nk_flags nk_convert(struct nk_context*, struct nk_buffer *cmds, struct nk_buffer *vertices, struct nk_buffer *elements, const struct nk_convert_config*);
   1288 
   1289 /**
   1290  * \brief Returns a draw vertex command buffer iterator to iterate over the vertex draw command buffer
   1291  *
   1292  * \details
   1293  * ```c
   1294  * const struct nk_draw_command* nk__draw_begin(const struct nk_context*, const struct nk_buffer*);
   1295  * ```
   1296  *
   1297  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1298  * \param[in] buf     | Must point to an previously by `nk_convert` filled out vertex draw command buffer
   1299  *
   1300  * \returns vertex draw command pointer pointing to the first command inside the vertex draw command buffer
   1301  */
   1302 NK_API const struct nk_draw_command* nk__draw_begin(const struct nk_context*, const struct nk_buffer*);
   1303 
   1304 /**
   1305 
   1306  * # # nk__draw_end
   1307  * \returns the vertex draw command at the end of the vertex draw command buffer
   1308  *
   1309  * ```c
   1310  * const struct nk_draw_command* nk__draw_end(const struct nk_context *ctx, const struct nk_buffer *buf);
   1311  * ```
   1312  *
   1313  * Parameter   | Description
   1314  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   1315  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1316  * \param[in] buf     | Must point to an previously by `nk_convert` filled out vertex draw command buffer
   1317  *
   1318  * \returns vertex draw command pointer pointing to the end of the last vertex draw command inside the vertex draw command buffer
   1319 
   1320  */
   1321 NK_API const struct nk_draw_command* nk__draw_end(const struct nk_context*, const struct nk_buffer*);
   1322 
   1323 /**
   1324  * # # nk__draw_next
   1325  * Increments the vertex draw command buffer iterator
   1326  *
   1327  * ```c
   1328  * const struct nk_draw_command* nk__draw_next(const struct nk_draw_command*, const struct nk_buffer*, const struct nk_context*);
   1329  * ```
   1330  *
   1331  * Parameter   | Description
   1332  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   1333  * \param[in] cmd     | Must point to an previously either by `nk__draw_begin` or `nk__draw_next` returned vertex draw command
   1334  * \param[in] buf     | Must point to an previously by `nk_convert` filled out vertex draw command buffer
   1335  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1336  *
   1337  * \returns vertex draw command pointer pointing to the end of the last vertex draw command inside the vertex draw command buffer
   1338 
   1339  */
   1340 NK_API const struct nk_draw_command* nk__draw_next(const struct nk_draw_command*, const struct nk_buffer*, const struct nk_context*);
   1341 
   1342 /**
   1343  * # # nk_draw_foreach
   1344  * Iterates over each vertex draw command inside a vertex draw command buffer
   1345  *
   1346  * ```c
   1347  * #define nk_draw_foreach(cmd,ctx, b)
   1348  * ```
   1349  *
   1350  * Parameter   | Description
   1351  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   1352  * \param[in] cmd     | `nk_draw_command`iterator set to NULL
   1353  * \param[in] buf     | Must point to an previously by `nk_convert` filled out vertex draw command buffer
   1354  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct at the end of a frame
   1355  */
   1356 
   1357 #define nk_draw_foreach(cmd,ctx, b) for((cmd)=nk__draw_begin(ctx, b); (cmd)!=0; (cmd)=nk__draw_next(cmd, b, ctx))
   1358 #endif

   1360 /** =============================================================================
   1361  *
   1362  *                                  WINDOW
   1363  *
   1364  * =============================================================================*/
   1365 /**
   1366  * \page Window
   1367  * Windows are the main persistent state used inside nuklear and are life time
   1368  * controlled by simply "retouching" (i.e. calling) each window each frame.
   1369  * All widgets inside nuklear can only be added inside the function pair `nk_begin_xxx`
   1370  * and `nk_end`. Calling any widgets outside these two functions will result in an
   1371  * assert in debug or no state change in release mode.<br /><br />
   1372  *
   1373  * Each window holds frame persistent state like position, size, flags, state tables,
   1374  * and some garbage collected internal persistent widget state. Each window
   1375  * is linked into a window stack list which determines the drawing and overlapping
   1376  * order. The topmost window thereby is the currently active window.<br /><br />
   1377  *
   1378  * To change window position inside the stack occurs either automatically by
   1379  * user input by being clicked on or programmatically by calling `nk_window_focus`.
   1380  * Windows by default are visible unless explicitly being defined with flag
   1381  * `NK_WINDOW_HIDDEN`, the user clicked the close button on windows with flag
   1382  * `NK_WINDOW_CLOSABLE` or if a window was explicitly hidden by calling
   1383  * `nk_window_show`. To explicitly close and destroy a window call `nk_window_close`.<br /><br />
   1384  *
   1385  * # Usage
   1386  * To create and keep a window you have to call one of the two `nk_begin_xxx`
   1387  * functions to start window declarations and `nk_end` at the end. Furthermore it
   1388  * is recommended to check the return value of `nk_begin_xxx` and only process
   1389  * widgets inside the window if the value is not 0. Either way you have to call
   1390  * `nk_end` at the end of window declarations. Furthermore, do not attempt to
   1391  * nest `nk_begin_xxx` calls which will hopefully result in an assert or if not
   1392  * in a segmentation fault.
   1393  *
   1394  * ```c
   1395  * if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   1396  *     // [... widgets ...]
   1397  * }
   1398  * nk_end(ctx);
   1399  * ```
   1400  *
   1401  * In the grand concept window and widget declarations need to occur after input
   1402  * handling and before drawing to screen. Not doing so can result in higher
   1403  * latency or at worst invalid behavior. Furthermore make sure that `nk_clear`
   1404  * is called at the end of the frame. While nuklear's default platform backends
   1405  * already call `nk_clear` for you if you write your own backend not calling
   1406  * `nk_clear` can cause asserts or even worse undefined behavior.
   1407  *
   1408  * ```c
   1409  * struct nk_context ctx;
   1410  * nk_init_xxx(&ctx, ...);
   1411  * while (1) {
   1412  *     Event evt;
   1413  *     nk_input_begin(&ctx);
   1414  *     while (GetEvent(&evt)) {
   1415  *         if (evt.type == MOUSE_MOVE)
   1416  *             nk_input_motion(&ctx, evt.motion.x, evt.motion.y);
   1417  *         else if (evt.type == [...]) {
   1418  *             nk_input_xxx(...);
   1419  *         }
   1420  *     }
   1421  *     nk_input_end(&ctx);
   1422  *
   1423  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   1424  *         //[...]
   1425  *     }
   1426  *     nk_end(ctx);
   1427  *
   1428  *     const struct nk_command *cmd = 0;
   1429  *     nk_foreach(cmd, &ctx) {
   1430  *     case NK_COMMAND_LINE:
   1431  *         your_draw_line_function(...)
   1432  *         break;
   1433  *     case NK_COMMAND_RECT
   1434  *         your_draw_rect_function(...)
   1435  *         break;
   1436  *     case //...:
   1437  *         //[...]
   1438  *     }
   1439  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
   1440  * }
   1441  * nk_free(&ctx);
   1442  * ```
   1443  *
   1444  * # Reference
   1445  * Function                            | Description
   1446  * ------------------------------------|----------------------------------------
   1447  * \ref nk_begin                            | Starts a new window; needs to be called every frame for every window (unless hidden) or otherwise the window gets removed
   1448  * \ref nk_begin_titled                     | Extended window start with separated title and identifier to allow multiple windows with same name but not title
   1449  * \ref nk_end                              | Needs to be called at the end of the window building process to process scaling, scrollbars and general cleanup
   1450  *
   1451  * \ref nk_window_find                      | Finds and returns the window with give name
   1452  * \ref nk_window_get_bounds                | Returns a rectangle with screen position and size of the currently processed window.
   1453  * \ref nk_window_get_position              | Returns the position of the currently processed window
   1454  * \ref nk_window_get_size                  | Returns the size with width and height of the currently processed window
   1455  * \ref nk_window_get_width                 | Returns the width of the currently processed window
   1456  * \ref nk_window_get_height                | Returns the height of the currently processed window
   1457  * \ref nk_window_get_panel                 | Returns the underlying panel which contains all processing state of the current window
   1458  * \ref nk_window_get_content_region        | Returns the position and size of the currently visible and non-clipped space inside the currently processed window
   1459  * \ref nk_window_get_content_region_min    | Returns the upper rectangle position of the currently visible and non-clipped space inside the currently processed window
   1460  * \ref nk_window_get_content_region_max    | Returns the upper rectangle position of the currently visible and non-clipped space inside the currently processed window
   1461  * \ref nk_window_get_content_region_size   | Returns the size of the currently visible and non-clipped space inside the currently processed window
   1462  * \ref nk_window_get_canvas                | Returns the draw command buffer. Can be used to draw custom widgets
   1463  * \ref nk_window_get_scroll                | Gets the scroll offset of the current window
   1464  * \ref nk_window_has_focus                 | Returns if the currently processed window is currently active
   1465  * \ref nk_window_is_collapsed              | Returns if the window with given name is currently minimized/collapsed
   1466  * \ref nk_window_is_closed                 | Returns if the currently processed window was closed
   1467  * \ref nk_window_is_hidden                 | Returns if the currently processed window was hidden
   1468  * \ref nk_window_is_active                 | Same as nk_window_has_focus for some reason
   1469  * \ref nk_window_is_hovered                | Returns if the currently processed window is currently being hovered by mouse
   1470  * \ref nk_window_is_any_hovered            | Return if any window currently hovered
   1471  * \ref nk_item_is_any_active               | Returns if any window or widgets is currently hovered or active
   1472 //
   1473  * \ref nk_window_set_bounds                | Updates position and size of the currently processed window
   1474  * \ref nk_window_set_position              | Updates position of the currently process window
   1475  * \ref nk_window_set_size                  | Updates the size of the currently processed window
   1476  * \ref nk_window_set_focus                 | Set the currently processed window as active window
   1477  * \ref nk_window_set_scroll                | Sets the scroll offset of the current window
   1478 //
   1479  * \ref nk_window_close                     | Closes the window with given window name which deletes the window at the end of the frame
   1480  * \ref nk_window_collapse                  | Collapses the window with given window name
   1481  * \ref nk_window_collapse_if               | Collapses the window with given window name if the given condition was met
   1482  * \ref nk_window_show                      | Hides a visible or reshows a hidden window
   1483  * \ref nk_window_show_if                   | Hides/shows a window depending on condition
   1484 
   1485  * # nk_panel_flags
   1486  * Flag                        | Description
   1487  * ----------------------------|----------------------------------------
   1488  * NK_WINDOW_BORDER            | Draws a border around the window to visually separate window from the background
   1489  * NK_WINDOW_MOVABLE           | The movable flag indicates that a window can be moved by user input or by dragging the window header
   1490  * NK_WINDOW_SCALABLE          | The scalable flag indicates that a window can be scaled by user input by dragging a scaler icon at the button of the window
   1491  * NK_WINDOW_CLOSABLE          | Adds a closable icon into the header
   1492  * NK_WINDOW_MINIMIZABLE       | Adds a minimize icon into the header
   1493  * NK_WINDOW_NO_SCROLLBAR      | Removes the scrollbar from the window
   1494  * NK_WINDOW_TITLE             | Forces a header at the top at the window showing the title
   1495  * NK_WINDOW_SCROLL_AUTO_HIDE  | Automatically hides the window scrollbar if no user interaction: also requires delta time in `nk_context` to be set each frame
   1496  * NK_WINDOW_BACKGROUND        | Always keep window in the background
   1497  * NK_WINDOW_SCALE_LEFT        | Puts window scaler in the left-bottom corner instead right-bottom
   1498  * NK_WINDOW_NO_INPUT          | Prevents window of scaling, moving or getting focus
   1499  *
   1500  * # nk_collapse_states
   1501  * State           | Description
   1502  * ----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   1503  * NK_MINIMIZED| UI section is collapsed and not visible until maximized
   1504  * NK_MAXIMIZED| UI section is extended and visible until minimized
   1505  */
   1506 
   1507 enum nk_panel_flags {
   1508     NK_WINDOW_BORDER            = NK_FLAG(0),
   1509     NK_WINDOW_MOVABLE           = NK_FLAG(1),
   1510     NK_WINDOW_SCALABLE          = NK_FLAG(2),
   1511     NK_WINDOW_CLOSABLE          = NK_FLAG(3),
   1512     NK_WINDOW_MINIMIZABLE       = NK_FLAG(4),
   1513     NK_WINDOW_NO_SCROLLBAR      = NK_FLAG(5),
   1514     NK_WINDOW_TITLE             = NK_FLAG(6),
   1515     NK_WINDOW_SCROLL_AUTO_HIDE  = NK_FLAG(7),
   1516     NK_WINDOW_BACKGROUND        = NK_FLAG(8),
   1517     NK_WINDOW_SCALE_LEFT        = NK_FLAG(9),
   1518     NK_WINDOW_NO_INPUT          = NK_FLAG(10)
   1519 };
   1520 
   1521 /**
   1522  * # # nk_begin
   1523  * Starts a new window; needs to be called every frame for every
   1524  * window (unless hidden) or otherwise the window gets removed
   1525  *
   1526  * ```c
   1527  * nk_bool nk_begin(struct nk_context *ctx, const char *title, struct nk_rect bounds, nk_flags flags);
   1528  * ```
   1529  *
   1530  * Parameter   | Description
   1531  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   1532  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   1533  * \param[in] title   | Window title and identifier. Needs to be persistent over frames to identify the window
   1534  * \param[in] bounds  | Initial position and window size. However if you do not define `NK_WINDOW_SCALABLE` or `NK_WINDOW_MOVABLE` you can set window position and size every frame
   1535  * \param[in] flags   | Window flags defined in the nk_panel_flags section with a number of different window behaviors
   1536  *
   1537  * \returns `true(1)` if the window can be filled up with widgets from this point
   1538  * until `nk_end` or `false(0)` otherwise for example if minimized
   1539 
   1540  */
   1541 NK_API nk_bool nk_begin(struct nk_context *ctx, const char *title, struct nk_rect bounds, nk_flags flags);
   1542 
   1543 /**
   1544  * # # nk_begin_titled
   1545  * Extended window start with separated title and identifier to allow multiple
   1546  * windows with same title but not name
   1547  *
   1548  * ```c
   1549  * nk_bool nk_begin_titled(struct nk_context *ctx, const char *name, const char *title, struct nk_rect bounds, nk_flags flags);
   1550  * ```
   1551  *
   1552  * Parameter   | Description
   1553  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   1554  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   1555  * \param[in] name    | Window identifier. Needs to be persistent over frames to identify the window
   1556  * \param[in] title   | Window title displayed inside header if flag `NK_WINDOW_TITLE` or either `NK_WINDOW_CLOSABLE` or `NK_WINDOW_MINIMIZED` was set
   1557  * \param[in] bounds  | Initial position and window size. However if you do not define `NK_WINDOW_SCALABLE` or `NK_WINDOW_MOVABLE` you can set window position and size every frame
   1558  * \param[in] flags   | Window flags defined in the nk_panel_flags section with a number of different window behaviors
   1559  *
   1560  * \returns `true(1)` if the window can be filled up with widgets from this point
   1561  * until `nk_end` or `false(0)` otherwise for example if minimized
   1562 
   1563  */

   2156 /* =============================================================================
   2157  *
   2158  *                                  LAYOUT
   2159  *
   2160  * =============================================================================*/
   2161 /**
   2162  * \page Layouting
   2163  * Layouting in general describes placing widget inside a window with position and size.
   2164  * While in this particular implementation there are five different APIs for layouting
   2165  * each with different trade offs between control and ease of use. <br /><br />
   2166  *
   2167  * All layouting methods in this library are based around the concept of a row.
   2168  * A row has a height the window content grows by and a number of columns and each
   2169  * layouting method specifies how each widget is placed inside the row.
   2170  * After a row has been allocated by calling a layouting functions and then
   2171  * filled with widgets will advance an internal pointer over the allocated row. <br /><br />
   2172  *
   2173  * To actually define a layout you just call the appropriate layouting function
   2174  * and each subsequent widget call will place the widget as specified. Important
   2175  * here is that if you define more widgets then columns defined inside the layout
   2176  * functions it will allocate the next row without you having to make another layouting <br /><br />
   2177  * call.
   2178  *
   2179  * Biggest limitation with using all these APIs outside the `nk_layout_space_xxx` API
   2180  * is that you have to define the row height for each. However the row height
   2181  * often depends on the height of the font. <br /><br />
   2182  *
   2183  * To fix that internally nuklear uses a minimum row height that is set to the
   2184  * height plus padding of currently active font and overwrites the row height
   2185  * value if zero. <br /><br />
   2186  *
   2187  * If you manually want to change the minimum row height then
   2188  * use nk_layout_set_min_row_height, and use nk_layout_reset_min_row_height to
   2189  * reset it back to be derived from font height. <br /><br />
   2190  *
   2191  * Also if you change the font in nuklear it will automatically change the minimum
   2192  * row height for you and. This means if you change the font but still want
   2193  * a minimum row height smaller than the font you have to repush your value. <br /><br />
   2194  *
   2195  * For actually more advanced UI I would even recommend using the `nk_layout_space_xxx`
   2196  * layouting method in combination with a cassowary constraint solver (there are
   2197  * some versions on github with permissive license model) to take over all control over widget
   2198  * layouting yourself. However for quick and dirty layouting using all the other layouting
   2199  * functions should be fine.
   2200  *
   2201  * # Usage
   2202  * 1.  __nk_layout_row_dynamic__<br /><br />
   2203  *     The easiest layouting function is `nk_layout_row_dynamic`. It provides each
   2204  *     widgets with same horizontal space inside the row and dynamically grows
   2205  *     if the owning window grows in width. So the number of columns dictates
   2206  *     the size of each widget dynamically by formula:
   2207  *
   2208  *     ```c
   2209  *     widget_width = (window_width - padding - spacing) * (1/column_count)
   2210  *     ```
   2211  *
   2212  *     Just like all other layouting APIs if you define more widget than columns this
   2213  *     library will allocate a new row and keep all layouting parameters previously
   2214  *     defined.
   2215  *
   2216  *     ```c
   2217  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   2218  *         // first row with height: 30 composed of two widgets
   2219  *         nk_layout_row_dynamic(&ctx, 30, 2);
   2220  *         nk_widget(...);
   2221  *         nk_widget(...);
   2222  *         //
   2223  *         // second row with same parameter as defined above
   2224  *         nk_widget(...);
   2225  *         nk_widget(...);
   2226  *         //
   2227  *         // third row uses 0 for height which will use auto layouting
   2228  *         nk_layout_row_dynamic(&ctx, 0, 2);
   2229  *         nk_widget(...);
   2230  *         nk_widget(...);
   2231  *     }
   2232  *     nk_end(...);
   2233  *     ```
   2234  *
   2235  * 2.  __nk_layout_row_static__<br /><br />
   2236  *     Another easy layouting function is `nk_layout_row_static`. It provides each
   2237  *     widget with same horizontal pixel width inside the row and does not grow
   2238  *     if the owning window scales smaller or bigger.
   2239  *
   2240  *     ```c
   2241  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   2242  *         // first row with height: 30 composed of two widgets with width: 80
   2243  *         nk_layout_row_static(&ctx, 30, 80, 2);
   2244  *         nk_widget(...);
   2245  *         nk_widget(...);
   2246  *         //
   2247  *         // second row with same parameter as defined above
   2248  *         nk_widget(...);
   2249  *         nk_widget(...);
   2250  *         //
   2251  *         // third row uses 0 for height which will use auto layouting
   2252  *         nk_layout_row_static(&ctx, 0, 80, 2);
   2253  *         nk_widget(...);
   2254  *         nk_widget(...);
   2255  *     }
   2256  *     nk_end(...);
   2257  *     ```
   2258  *
   2259  * 3.  __nk_layout_row_xxx__<br /><br />
   2260  *     A little bit more advanced layouting API are functions `nk_layout_row_begin`,
   2261  *     `nk_layout_row_push` and `nk_layout_row_end`. They allow to directly
   2262  *     specify each column pixel or window ratio in a row. It supports either
   2263  *     directly setting per column pixel width or widget window ratio but not
   2264  *     both. Furthermore it is a immediate mode API so each value is directly
   2265  *     pushed before calling a widget. Therefore the layout is not automatically
   2266  *     repeating like the last two layouting functions.
   2267  *
   2268  *     ```c
   2269  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   2270  *         // first row with height: 25 composed of two widgets with width 60 and 40
   2271  *         nk_layout_row_begin(ctx, NK_STATIC, 25, 2);
   2272  *         nk_layout_row_push(ctx, 60);
   2273  *         nk_widget(...);
   2274  *         nk_layout_row_push(ctx, 40);
   2275  *         nk_widget(...);
   2276  *         nk_layout_row_end(ctx);
   2277  *         //
   2278  *         // second row with height: 25 composed of two widgets with window ratio 0.25 and 0.75
   2279  *         nk_layout_row_begin(ctx, NK_DYNAMIC, 25, 2);
   2280  *         nk_layout_row_push(ctx, 0.25f);
   2281  *         nk_widget(...);
   2282  *         nk_layout_row_push(ctx, 0.75f);
   2283  *         nk_widget(...);
   2284  *         nk_layout_row_end(ctx);
   2285  *         //
   2286  *         // third row with auto generated height: composed of two widgets with window ratio 0.25 and 0.75
   2287  *         nk_layout_row_begin(ctx, NK_DYNAMIC, 0, 2);
   2288  *         nk_layout_row_push(ctx, 0.25f);
   2289  *         nk_widget(...);
   2290  *         nk_layout_row_push(ctx, 0.75f);
   2291  *         nk_widget(...);
   2292  *         nk_layout_row_end(ctx);
   2293  *     }
   2294  *     nk_end(...);
   2295  *     ```
   2296  *
   2297  * 4.  __nk_layout_row__<br /><br />
   2298  *     The array counterpart to API nk_layout_row_xxx is the single nk_layout_row
   2299  *     functions. Instead of pushing either pixel or window ratio for every widget
   2300  *     it allows to define it by array. The trade of for less control is that
   2301  *     `nk_layout_row` is automatically repeating. Otherwise the behavior is the
   2302  *     same.
   2303  *
   2304  *     ```c
   2305  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   2306  *         // two rows with height: 30 composed of two widgets with width 60 and 40
   2307  *         const float ratio[] = {60,40};
   2308  *         nk_layout_row(ctx, NK_STATIC, 30, 2, ratio);
   2309  *         nk_widget(...);
   2310  *         nk_widget(...);
   2311  *         nk_widget(...);
   2312  *         nk_widget(...);
   2313  *         //
   2314  *         // two rows with height: 30 composed of two widgets with window ratio 0.25 and 0.75
   2315  *         const float ratio[] = {0.25, 0.75};
   2316  *         nk_layout_row(ctx, NK_DYNAMIC, 30, 2, ratio);
   2317  *         nk_widget(...);
   2318  *         nk_widget(...);
   2319  *         nk_widget(...);
   2320  *         nk_widget(...);
   2321  *         //
   2322  *         // two rows with auto generated height composed of two widgets with window ratio 0.25 and 0.75
   2323  *         const float ratio[] = {0.25, 0.75};
   2324  *         nk_layout_row(ctx, NK_DYNAMIC, 30, 2, ratio);
   2325  *         nk_widget(...);
   2326  *         nk_widget(...);
   2327  *         nk_widget(...);
   2328  *         nk_widget(...);
   2329  *     }
   2330  *     nk_end(...);
   2331  *     ```
   2332  *
   2333  * 5.  __nk_layout_row_template_xxx__<br /><br />
   2334  *     The most complex and second most flexible API is a simplified flexbox version without
   2335  *     line wrapping and weights for dynamic widgets. It is an immediate mode API but
   2336  *     unlike `nk_layout_row_xxx` it has auto repeat behavior and needs to be called
   2337  *     before calling the templated widgets.
   2338  *     The row template layout has three different per widget size specifier. The first
   2339  *     one is the `nk_layout_row_template_push_static`  with fixed widget pixel width.
   2340  *     They do not grow if the row grows and will always stay the same.
   2341  *     The second size specifier is `nk_layout_row_template_push_variable`
   2342  *     which defines a minimum widget size but it also can grow if more space is available
   2343  *     not taken by other widgets.
   2344  *     Finally there are dynamic widgets with `nk_layout_row_template_push_dynamic`
   2345  *     which are completely flexible and unlike variable widgets can even shrink
   2346  *     to zero if not enough space is provided.
   2347  *
   2348  *     ```c
   2349  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   2350  *         // two rows with height: 30 composed of three widgets
   2351  *         nk_layout_row_template_begin(ctx, 30);
   2352  *         nk_layout_row_template_push_dynamic(ctx);
   2353  *         nk_layout_row_template_push_variable(ctx, 80);
   2354  *         nk_layout_row_template_push_static(ctx, 80);
   2355  *         nk_layout_row_template_end(ctx);
   2356  *         //
   2357  *         // first row
   2358  *         nk_widget(...); // dynamic widget can go to zero if not enough space
   2359  *         nk_widget(...); // variable widget with min 80 pixel but can grow bigger if enough space
   2360  *         nk_widget(...); // static widget with fixed 80 pixel width
   2361  *         //
   2362  *         // second row same layout
   2363  *         nk_widget(...);
   2364  *         nk_widget(...);
   2365  *         nk_widget(...);
   2366  *     }
   2367  *     nk_end(...);
   2368  *     ```
   2369  *
   2370  * 6.  __nk_layout_space_xxx__<br /><br />
   2371  *     Finally the most flexible API directly allows you to place widgets inside the
   2372  *     window. The space layout API is an immediate mode API which does not support
   2373  *     row auto repeat and directly sets position and size of a widget. Position
   2374  *     and size hereby can be either specified as ratio of allocated space or
   2375  *     allocated space local position and pixel size. Since this API is quite
   2376  *     powerful there are a number of utility functions to get the available space
   2377  *     and convert between local allocated space and screen space.
   2378  *
   2379  *     ```c
   2380  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   2381  *         // static row with height: 500 (you can set column count to INT_MAX if you don't want to be bothered)
   2382  *         nk_layout_space_begin(ctx, NK_STATIC, 500, INT_MAX);
   2383  *         nk_layout_space_push(ctx, nk_rect(0,0,150,200));
   2384  *         nk_widget(...);
   2385  *         nk_layout_space_push(ctx, nk_rect(200,200,100,200));
   2386  *         nk_widget(...);
   2387  *         nk_layout_space_end(ctx);
   2388  *         //
   2389  *         // dynamic row with height: 500 (you can set column count to INT_MAX if you don't want to be bothered)
   2390  *         nk_layout_space_begin(ctx, NK_DYNAMIC, 500, INT_MAX);
   2391  *         nk_layout_space_push(ctx, nk_rect(0.5,0.5,0.1,0.1));
   2392  *         nk_widget(...);
   2393  *         nk_layout_space_push(ctx, nk_rect(0.7,0.6,0.1,0.1));
   2394  *         nk_widget(...);
   2395  *     }
   2396  *     nk_end(...);
   2397  *     ```
   2398  *
   2399  * # Reference
   2400  * Function                                     | Description
   2401  * ---------------------------------------------|------------------------------------
   2402  * \ref nk_layout_set_min_row_height            | Set the currently used minimum row height to a specified value
   2403  * \ref nk_layout_reset_min_row_height          | Resets the currently used minimum row height to font height
   2404  * \ref nk_layout_widget_bounds                 | Calculates current width a static layout row can fit inside a window
   2405  * \ref nk_layout_ratio_from_pixel              | Utility functions to calculate window ratio from pixel size
   2406  * \ref nk_layout_row_dynamic                   | Current layout is divided into n same sized growing columns
   2407  * \ref nk_layout_row_static                    | Current layout is divided into n same fixed sized columns
   2408  * \ref nk_layout_row_begin                     | Starts a new row with given height and number of columns
   2409  * \ref nk_layout_row_push                      | Pushes another column with given size or window ratio
   2410  * \ref nk_layout_row_end                       | Finished previously started row
   2411  * \ref nk_layout_row                           | Specifies row columns in array as either window ratio or size
   2412  * \ref nk_layout_row_template_begin            | Begins the row template declaration
   2413  * \ref nk_layout_row_template_push_dynamic     | Adds a dynamic column that dynamically grows and can go to zero if not enough space
   2414  * \ref nk_layout_row_template_push_variable    | Adds a variable column that dynamically grows but does not shrink below specified pixel width
   2415  * \ref nk_layout_row_template_push_static      | Adds a static column that does not grow and will always have the same size
   2416  * \ref nk_layout_row_template_end              | Marks the end of the row template
   2417  * \ref nk_layout_space_begin                   | Begins a new layouting space that allows to specify each widgets position and size
   2418  * \ref nk_layout_space_push                    | Pushes position and size of the next widget in own coordinate space either as pixel or ratio
   2419  * \ref nk_layout_space_end                     | Marks the end of the layouting space
   2420  * \ref nk_layout_space_bounds                  | Callable after nk_layout_space_begin and returns total space allocated
   2421  * \ref nk_layout_space_to_screen               | Converts vector from nk_layout_space coordinate space into screen space
   2422  * \ref nk_layout_space_to_local                | Converts vector from screen space into nk_layout_space coordinates
   2423  * \ref nk_layout_space_rect_to_screen          | Converts rectangle from nk_layout_space coordinate space into screen space
   2424  * \ref nk_layout_space_rect_to_local           | Converts rectangle from screen space into nk_layout_space coordinates
   2425  */
   2426
