   2791 /** =============================================================================
   2792  *
   2793  *                                  GROUP
   2794  *
   2795  * =============================================================================*/
   2796 /**
   2797  * \page Groups
   2798  * Groups are basically windows inside windows. They allow to subdivide space
   2799  * in a window to layout widgets as a group. Almost all more complex widget
   2800  * layouting requirements can be solved using groups and basic layouting
   2801  * fuctionality. Groups just like windows are identified by an unique name and
   2802  * internally keep track of scrollbar offsets by default. However additional
   2803  * versions are provided to directly manage the scrollbar.
   2804  *
   2805  * # Usage
   2806  * To create a group you have to call one of the three `nk_group_begin_xxx`
   2807  * functions to start group declarations and `nk_group_end` at the end. Furthermore it
   2808  * is required to check the return value of `nk_group_begin_xxx` and only process
   2809  * widgets inside the window if the value is not 0.
   2810  * Nesting groups is possible and even encouraged since many layouting schemes
   2811  * can only be achieved by nesting. Groups, unlike windows, need `nk_group_end`
   2812  * to be only called if the corresponding `nk_group_begin_xxx` call does not return 0:
   2813  *
   2814  * ```c
   2815  * if (nk_group_begin_xxx(ctx, ...) {
   2816  *     // [... widgets ...]
   2817  *     nk_group_end(ctx);
   2818  * }
   2819  * ```
   2820  *
   2821  * In the grand concept groups can be called after starting a window
   2822  * with `nk_begin_xxx` and before calling `nk_end`:
   2823  *
   2824  * ```c
   2825  * struct nk_context ctx;
   2826  * nk_init_xxx(&ctx, ...);
   2827  * while (1) {
   2828  *     // Input
   2829  *     Event evt;
   2830  *     nk_input_begin(&ctx);
   2831  *     while (GetEvent(&evt)) {
   2832  *         if (evt.type == MOUSE_MOVE)
   2833  *             nk_input_motion(&ctx, evt.motion.x, evt.motion.y);
   2834  *         else if (evt.type == [...]) {
   2835  *             nk_input_xxx(...);
   2836  *         }
   2837  *     }
   2838  *     nk_input_end(&ctx);
   2839  *     //
   2840  *     // Window
   2841  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   2842  *         // [...widgets...]
   2843  *         nk_layout_row_dynamic(...);
   2844  *         if (nk_group_begin_xxx(ctx, ...) {
   2845  *             //[... widgets ...]
   2846  *             nk_group_end(ctx);
   2847  *         }
   2848  *     }
   2849  *     nk_end(ctx);
   2850  *     //
   2851  *     // Draw
   2852  *     const struct nk_command *cmd = 0;
   2853  *     nk_foreach(cmd, &ctx) {
   2854  *     switch (cmd->type) {
   2855  *     case NK_COMMAND_LINE:
   2856  *         your_draw_line_function(...)
   2857  *         break;
   2858  *     case NK_COMMAND_RECT
   2859  *         your_draw_rect_function(...)
   2860  *         break;
   2861  *     case ...:
   2862  *         // [...]
   2863  *     }
   2864  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
   2865  * }
   2866  * nk_free(&ctx);
   2867  * ```
   2868  * # Reference
   2869  * Function                        | Description
   2870  * --------------------------------|-------------------------------------------
   2871  * \ref nk_group_begin                  | Start a new group with internal scrollbar handling
   2872  * \ref nk_group_begin_titled           | Start a new group with separated name and title and internal scrollbar handling
   2873  * \ref nk_group_end                    | Ends a group. Should only be called if nk_group_begin returned non-zero
   2874  * \ref nk_group_scrolled_offset_begin  | Start a new group with manual separated handling of scrollbar x- and y-offset
   2875  * \ref nk_group_scrolled_begin         | Start a new group with manual scrollbar handling
   2876  * \ref nk_group_scrolled_end           | Ends a group with manual scrollbar handling. Should only be called if nk_group_begin returned non-zero
   2877  * \ref nk_group_get_scroll             | Gets the scroll offset for the given group
   2878  * \ref nk_group_set_scroll             | Sets the scroll offset for the given group
   2879  */
   2880 
   2881  /**
   2882  * \brief Starts a new widget group. Requires a previous layouting function to specify a pos/size.
   2883  * ```c
   2884  * nk_bool nk_group_begin(struct nk_context*, const char *title, nk_flags);
   2885  * ```
   2886  *
   2887  * Parameter   | Description
   2888  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   2889  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   2890  * \param[in] title   | Must be an unique identifier for this group that is also used for the group header
   2891  * \param[in] flags   | Window flags defined in the nk_panel_flags section with a number of different group behaviors
   2892  *
   2893  * \returns `true(1)` if visible and fillable with widgets or `false(0)` otherwise
   2894  */
   2895 NK_API nk_bool nk_group_begin(struct nk_context*, const char *title, nk_flags);
   2896 
   2897  /**
   2898  * \brief Starts a new widget group. Requires a previous layouting function to specify a pos/size.

   2902  *
   2903  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   2904  * \param[in] id      | Must be an unique identifier for this group
   2905  * \param[in] title   | Group header title
   2906  * \param[in] flags   | Window flags defined in the nk_panel_flags section with a number of different group behaviors
   2907  *

   2911

   2993 /**

   2996  * ```c

   3009 /** =============================================================================
   3010  *
   3011  *                                  TREE
   3012  *
   3013  * =============================================================================*/
   3014 /**
   3015  * \page Tree
   3016  * Trees represent two different concept. First the concept of a collapsible
   3017  * UI section that can be either in a hidden or visible state. They allow the UI
   3018  * user to selectively minimize the current set of visible UI to comprehend.
   3019  * The second concept are tree widgets for visual UI representation of trees.<br /><br />
   3020  *
   3021  * Trees thereby can be nested for tree representations and multiple nested
   3022  * collapsible UI sections. All trees are started by calling of the
   3023  * `nk_tree_xxx_push_tree` functions and ended by calling one of the
   3024  * `nk_tree_xxx_pop_xxx()` functions. Each starting functions takes a title label
   3025  * and optionally an image to be displayed and the initial collapse state from
   3026  * the nk_collapse_states section.<br /><br />
   3027  *
   3028  * The runtime state of the tree is either stored outside the library by the caller
   3029  * or inside which requires a unique ID. The unique ID can either be generated
   3030  * automatically from `__FILE__` and `__LINE__` with function `nk_tree_push`,
   3031  * by `__FILE__` and a user provided ID generated for example by loop index with
   3032  * function `nk_tree_push_id` or completely provided from outside by user with
   3033  * function `nk_tree_push_hashed`.
   3034  *
   3035  * # Usage
   3036  * To create a tree you have to call one of the seven `nk_tree_xxx_push_xxx`
   3037  * functions to start a collapsible UI section and `nk_tree_xxx_pop` to mark the
   3038  * end.
   3039  * Each starting function will either return `false(0)` if the tree is collapsed
   3040  * or hidden and therefore does not need to be filled with content or `true(1)`
   3041  * if visible and required to be filled.
   3042  *
   3043  * !!! Note
   3044  *     The tree header does not require and layouting function and instead
   3045  *     calculates a auto height based on the currently used font size
   3046  *
   3047  * The tree ending functions only need to be called if the tree content is
   3048  * actually visible. So make sure the tree push function is guarded by `if`
   3049  * and the pop call is only taken if the tree is visible.
   3050  *
   3051  * ```c
   3052  * if (nk_tree_push(ctx, NK_TREE_TAB, "Tree", NK_MINIMIZED)) {
   3053  *     nk_layout_row_dynamic(...);
   3054  *     nk_widget(...);
   3055  *     nk_tree_pop(ctx);
   3056  * }
   3057  * ```
   3058  *
   3059  * # Reference
   3060  * Function                    | Description
   3061  * ----------------------------|-------------------------------------------
   3062  * nk_tree_push                | Start a collapsible UI section with internal state management
   3063  * nk_tree_push_id             | Start a collapsible UI section with internal state management callable in a look
   3064  * nk_tree_push_hashed         | Start a collapsible UI section with internal state management with full control over internal unique ID use to store state
   3065  * nk_tree_image_push          | Start a collapsible UI section with image and label header
   3066  * nk_tree_image_push_id       | Start a collapsible UI section with image and label header and internal state management callable in a look
   3067  * nk_tree_image_push_hashed   | Start a collapsible UI section with image and label header and internal state management with full control over internal unique ID use to store state
   3068  * nk_tree_pop                 | Ends a collapsible UI section
   3069  * nk_tree_state_push          | Start a collapsible UI section with external state management
   3070  * nk_tree_state_image_push    | Start a collapsible UI section with image and label header and external state management
   3071  * nk_tree_state_pop           | Ends a collapsabale UI section
   3072  *
   3073  * # nk_tree_type
   3074  * Flag            | Description
   3075  * ----------------|----------------------------------------
   3076  * NK_TREE_NODE    | Highlighted tree header to mark a collapsible UI section
   3077  * NK_TREE_TAB     | Non-highlighted tree header closer to tree representations
   3078  */
   3079 
   3080 /**
   3081  * # # nk_tree_push
   3082  * Starts a collapsible UI section with internal state management
   3083  * !!! \warning
   3084  *     To keep track of the runtime tree collapsible state this function uses
   3085  *     defines `__FILE__` and `__LINE__` to generate a unique ID. If you want
   3086  *     to call this function in a loop please use `nk_tree_push_id` or
   3087  *     `nk_tree_push_hashed` instead.
   3088  *
   3089  * ```c
   3090  * #define nk_tree_push(ctx, type, title, state)
   3091  * ```
   3092  *
   3093  * Parameter   | Description
   3094  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   3095  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   3096  * \param[in] type    | Value from the nk_tree_type section to visually mark a tree node header as either a collapseable UI section or tree node
   3097  * \param[in] title   | Label printed in the tree header
   3098  * \param[in] state   | Initial tree state value out of nk_collapse_states
   3099  *
   3100  * \returns `true(1)` if visible and fillable with widgets or `false(0)` otherwise
   3101  */
   3102 #define nk_tree_push(ctx, type, title, state) nk_tree_push_hashed(ctx, type, title, state, NK_FILE_LINE,nk_strlen(NK_FILE_LINE),__LINE__)
   3103 
   3104 /**
   3105  * # # nk_tree_push_id
   3106  * Starts a collapsible UI section with internal state management callable in a look
   3107  * ```c
   3108  * #define nk_tree_push_id(ctx, type, title, state, id)
   3109  * ```
   3110  *
   3111  * Parameter   | Description
   3112  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   3113  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   3114  * \param[in] type    | Value from the nk_tree_type section to visually mark a tree node header as either a collapseable UI section or tree node
   3115  * \param[in] title   | Label printed in the tree header
   3116  * \param[in] state   | Initial tree state value out of nk_collapse_states
   3117  * \param[in] id      | Loop counter index if this function is called in a loop
   3118  *
   3119  * \returns `true(1)` if visible and fillable with widgets or `false(0)` otherwise
   3120  */
   3121 #define nk_tree_push_id(ctx, type, title, state, id) nk_tree_push_hashed(ctx, type, title, state, NK_FILE_LINE,nk_strlen(NK_FILE_LINE),id)
   3122 
   3123 /**
   3124  * # # nk_tree_push_hashed
   3125  * Start a collapsible UI section with internal state management with full
   3126  * control over internal unique ID used to store state
   3127  * ```c
   3128  * nk_bool nk_tree_push_hashed(struct nk_context*, enum nk_tree_type, const char *title, enum nk_collapse_states initial_state, const char *hash, int len,int seed);
   3129  * ```
   3130  *
   3131  * Parameter   | Description
   3132  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   3133  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   3134  * \param[in] type    | Value from the nk_tree_type section to visually mark a tree node header as either a collapseable UI section or tree node
   3135  * \param[in] title   | Label printed in the tree header
   3136  * \param[in] state   | Initial tree state value out of nk_collapse_states
   3137  * \param[in] hash    | Memory block or string to generate the ID from
   3138  * \param[in] len     | Size of passed memory block or string in __hash__
   3139  * \param[in] seed    | Seeding value if this function is called in a loop or default to `0`
   3140  *
   3141  * \returns `true(1)` if visible and fillable with widgets or `false(0)` otherwise
   3142  */
   3143 NK_API nk_bool nk_tree_push_hashed(struct nk_context*, enum nk_tree_type, const char *title, enum nk_collapse_states initial_state, const char *hash, int len,int seed);
   3144 
   3145 /**
   3146  * # # nk_tree_image_push
   3147  * Start a collapsible UI section with image and label header
   3148  * !!! \warning
   3149  *     To keep track of the runtime tree collapsible state this function uses
   3150  *     defines `__FILE__` and `__LINE__` to generate a unique ID. If you want

   3153  *

   3156  * ```

   3159  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   3160  * \param[in] type    | Value from the nk_tree_type section to visually mark a tree node header as either a collapseable UI section or tree node
   3161  * \param[in] img     | Image to display inside the header on the left of the label
   3162  * \param[in] title   | Label printed in the tree header
   3163  * \param[in] state   | Initial tree state value out of nk_collapse_states
   3164  *
   3165  * \returns `true(1)` if visible and fillable with widgets or `false(0)` otherwise
   3166  */
   3167 #define nk_tree_image_push(ctx, type, img, title, state) nk_tree_image_push_hashed(ctx, type, img, title, state, NK_FILE_LINE,nk_strlen(NK_FILE_LINE),__LINE__)
   3168 
   3169 /**
   3170  * # # nk_tree_image_push_id
   3171  * Start a collapsible UI section with image and label header and internal state
   3172  * management callable in a look
   3173  *
   3174  * ```c

   3177  *

   3179  * ------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   3180  * \param[in] ctx     | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct
   3181  * \param[in] type    | Value from the nk_tree_type section to visually mark a tree node header as either a collapseable UI section or tree node
   3182  * \param[in] img     | Image to display inside the header on the left of the label
   3183  * \param[in] title   | Label printed in the tree header
   3184  * \param[in] state   | Initial tree state value out of nk_collapse_states

   3188  */
   3189 #define nk_tree_image_push_id(ctx, type, img, title, state, id) nk_tree_image_push_hashed(ctx, type, img, title, state, NK_FILE_LINE,nk_strlen(NK_FILE_LINE),id)

   3304 enum nk_widget_layout_states {
   3305     NK_WIDGET_INVALID, /**< The widget cannot be seen and is completely out of view */
   3306     NK_WIDGET_VALID,   /**< The widget is completely inside the window and can be updated and drawn */
   3307     NK_WIDGET_ROM,     /**< The widget is partially visible and cannot be updated */
   3308     NK_WIDGET_DISABLED /**< The widget is manually disabled and acts like NK_WIDGET_ROM */
   3309 };
   3310 enum nk_widget_states {
   3311     NK_WIDGET_STATE_MODIFIED    = NK_FLAG(1),
   3312     NK_WIDGET_STATE_INACTIVE    = NK_FLAG(2), /**!< widget is neither active nor hovered */
   3313     NK_WIDGET_STATE_ENTERED     = NK_FLAG(3), /**!< widget has been hovered on the current frame */
   3314     NK_WIDGET_STATE_HOVER       = NK_FLAG(4), /**!< widget is being hovered */
   3315     NK_WIDGET_STATE_ACTIVED     = NK_FLAG(5),/**!< widget is currently activated */
   3316     NK_WIDGET_STATE_LEFT        = NK_FLAG(6), /**!< widget is from this frame on not hovered anymore */
   3317     NK_WIDGET_STATE_HOVERED     = NK_WIDGET_STATE_HOVER|NK_WIDGET_STATE_MODIFIED, /**!< widget is being hovered */
   3318     NK_WIDGET_STATE_ACTIVE      = NK_WIDGET_STATE_ACTIVED|NK_WIDGET_STATE_MODIFIED /**!< widget is currently activated */
   3319 };
   3320 NK_API enum nk_widget_layout_states nk_widget(struct nk_rect*, const struct nk_context*);

   3484 /* =============================================================================
   3485  *
   3486  *                                  PROPERTIES
   3487  *
   3488  * =============================================================================*/
   3489 /**
   3490  * \page Properties
   3491  * Properties are the main value modification widgets in Nuklear. Changing a value
   3492  * can be achieved by dragging, adding/removing incremental steps on button click
   3493  * or by directly typing a number.
   3494  *
   3495  * # Usage
   3496  * Each property requires a unique name for identification that is also used for
   3497  * displaying a label. If you want to use the same name multiple times make sure
   3498  * add a '#' before your name. The '#' will not be shown but will generate a
   3499  * unique ID. Each property also takes in a minimum and maximum value. If you want
   3500  * to make use of the complete number range of a type just use the provided
   3501  * type limits from `limits.h`. For example `INT_MIN` and `INT_MAX` for
   3502  * `nk_property_int` and `nk_propertyi`. In additional each property takes in
   3503  * a increment value that will be added or subtracted if either the increment
   3504  * decrement button is clicked. Finally there is a value for increment per pixel
   3505  * dragged that is added or subtracted from the value.
   3506  *
   3507  * ```c
   3508  * int value = 0;
   3509  * struct nk_context ctx;
   3510  * nk_init_xxx(&ctx, ...);
   3511  * while (1) {
   3512  *     // Input
   3513  *     Event evt;
   3514  *     nk_input_begin(&ctx);
   3515  *     while (GetEvent(&evt)) {
   3516  *         if (evt.type == MOUSE_MOVE)
   3517  *             nk_input_motion(&ctx, evt.motion.x, evt.motion.y);
   3518  *         else if (evt.type == [...]) {
   3519  *             nk_input_xxx(...);
   3520  *         }
   3521  *     }
   3522  *     nk_input_end(&ctx);
   3523  *     //
   3524  *     // Window
   3525  *     if (nk_begin_xxx(...) {
   3526  *         // Property
   3527  *         nk_layout_row_dynamic(...);
   3528  *         nk_property_int(ctx, "ID", INT_MIN, &value, INT_MAX, 1, 1);
   3529  *     }
   3530  *     nk_end(ctx);
   3531  *     //
   3532  *     // Draw
   3533  *     const struct nk_command *cmd = 0;
   3534  *     nk_foreach(cmd, &ctx) {
   3535  *     switch (cmd->type) {
   3536  *     case NK_COMMAND_LINE:
   3537  *         your_draw_line_function(...)
   3538  *         break;
   3539  *     case NK_COMMAND_RECT
   3540  *         your_draw_rect_function(...)
   3541  *         break;
   3542  *     case ...:
   3543  *         // [...]
   3544  *     }
   3545  *     nk_clear(&ctx);
   3546  * }
   3547  * nk_free(&ctx);
   3548  * ```
   3549  *
   3550  * # Reference
   3551  * Function            | Description
   3552  * --------------------|-------------------------------------------
   3553  * \ref nk_property_int     | Integer property directly modifying a passed in value
   3554  * \ref nk_property_float   | Float property directly modifying a passed in value
   3555  * \ref nk_property_double  | Double property directly modifying a passed in value
   3556  * \ref nk_propertyi        | Integer property returning the modified int value
   3557  * \ref nk_propertyf        | Float property returning the modified float value
   3558  * \ref nk_propertyd        | Double property returning the modified double value
   3559  *
   3560 
   3561  * # # nk_property_int
   3562  * Integer property directly modifying a passed in value
   3563  * !!! \warning
   3564  *     To generate a unique property ID using the same label make sure to insert
   3565  *     a `#` at the beginning. It will not be shown but guarantees correct behavior.
   3566  *
   3567  * ```c
   3568  * void nk_property_int(struct nk_context *ctx, const char *name, int min, int *val, int max, int step, float inc_per_pixel);
   3569  * ```
   3570  *
   3571  * Parameter           | Description
   3572  * --------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   3573  * \param[in] ctx             | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct after calling a layouting function
   3574  * \param[in] name            | String used both as a label as well as a unique identifier
   3575  * \param[in] min             | Minimum value not allowed to be underflown
   3576  * \param[in] val             | Integer pointer to be modified
   3577  * \param[in] max             | Maximum value not allowed to be overflown
   3578  * \param[in] step            | Increment added and subtracted on increment and decrement button
   3579  * \param[in] inc_per_pixel   | Value per pixel added or subtracted on dragging
   3580  */
   3581 NK_API void nk_property_int(struct nk_context*, const char *name, int min, int *val, int max, int step, float inc_per_pixel);
   3582 
   3583 /**
   3584  * # # nk_property_float
   3585  * Float property directly modifying a passed in value
   3586  * !!! \warning
   3587  *     To generate a unique property ID using the same label make sure to insert
   3588  *     a `#` at the beginning. It will not be shown but guarantees correct behavior.
   3589  *
   3590  * ```c
   3591  * void nk_property_float(struct nk_context *ctx, const char *name, float min, float *val, float max, float step, float inc_per_pixel);
   3592  * ```
   3593  *
   3594  * Parameter           | Description
   3595  * --------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   3596  * \param[in] ctx             | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct after calling a layouting function
   3597  * \param[in] name            | String used both as a label as well as a unique identifier
   3598  * \param[in] min             | Minimum value not allowed to be underflown
   3599  * \param[in] val             | Float pointer to be modified
   3600  * \param[in] max             | Maximum value not allowed to be overflown
   3601  * \param[in] step            | Increment added and subtracted on increment and decrement button
   3602  * \param[in] inc_per_pixel   | Value per pixel added or subtracted on dragging
   3603  */
   3604 NK_API void nk_property_float(struct nk_context*, const char *name, float min, float *val, float max, float step, float inc_per_pixel);
   3605 
   3606 /**
   3607  * # # nk_property_double
   3608  * Double property directly modifying a passed in value
   3609  * !!! \warning
   3610  *     To generate a unique property ID using the same label make sure to insert
   3611  *     a `#` at the beginning. It will not be shown but guarantees correct behavior.
   3612  *
   3613  * ```c
   3614  * void nk_property_double(struct nk_context *ctx, const char *name, double min, double *val, double max, double step, double inc_per_pixel);
   3615  * ```
   3616  *
   3617  * Parameter           | Description
   3618  * --------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------
   3619  * \param[in] ctx             | Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct after calling a layouting function
   3620  * \param[in] name            | String used both as a label as well as a unique identifier
   3621  * \param[in] min             | Minimum value not allowed to be underflown
   3622  * \param[in] val             | Double pointer to be modified
   3623  * \param[in] max             | Maximum value not allowed to be overflown
   3624  * \param[in] step            | Increment added and subtracted on increment and decrement button
   3625  * \param[in] inc_per_pixel   | Value per pixel added or subtracted on dragging

   3627 NK_API void nk_property_double(struct nk_context*, const char *name, double min, double *val, double max, double step, float inc_per_pixel);
   3628 
   3629 /**
   3630  * # # nk_propertyi
   3631  * Integer property modifying a passed in value and returning the new value
   3632  * !!! \warning
   3633  *     To generate a unique property ID using the same label make sure to insert
   3634  *     a `#` at the beginning. It will not be shown but guarantees correct behavior.
   3635  *
   3636  * ```c
   3637  * int nk_propertyi(struct nk_context *ctx, const char *name, int min, int val, int max, int step, float inc_per_pixel);
   3638  * ```
   3639  *
   3640  * \param[in] ctx              Must point to an previously initialized `nk_context` struct after calling a layouting function
   3641  * \param[in] name             String used both as a label as well as a unique identifier
   3642  * \param[in] min              Minimum value not allowed to be underflown
   3643  * \param[in] val              Current integer value to be modified and returned
   3644  * \param[in] max              Maximum value not allowed to be overflown
   3645  * \param[in] step             Increment added and subtracted on increment and decrement button
   3646  * \param[in] inc_per_pixel    Value per pixel added or subtracted on dragging
   3647  *
   3648  * \returns the new modified integer value
   3649  */
   3650 NK_API int nk_propertyi(struct nk_context*, const char *name, int min, int val, int max, int step, float inc_per_pixel);
   3651

   3653  * # # nk_propertyf

   3703 enum nk_edit_flags {
   3704     NK_EDIT_DEFAULT                 = 0,
   3705     NK_EDIT_READ_ONLY               = NK_FLAG(0),
   3706     NK_EDIT_AUTO_SELECT             = NK_FLAG(1),
   3707     NK_EDIT_SIG_ENTER               = NK_FLAG(2),
   3708     NK_EDIT_ALLOW_TAB               = NK_FLAG(3),
   3709     NK_EDIT_NO_CURSOR               = NK_FLAG(4),
   3710     NK_EDIT_SELECTABLE              = NK_FLAG(5),
   3711     NK_EDIT_CLIPBOARD               = NK_FLAG(6),
   3712     NK_EDIT_CTRL_ENTER_NEWLINE      = NK_FLAG(7),
   3713     NK_EDIT_NO_HORIZONTAL_SCROLL    = NK_FLAG(8),
   3714     NK_EDIT_ALWAYS_INSERT_MODE      = NK_FLAG(9),
   3715     NK_EDIT_MULTILINE               = NK_FLAG(10),
   3716     NK_EDIT_GOTO_END_ON_ACTIVATE    = NK_FLAG(11)
   3717 };
   3718 enum nk_edit_types {
   3719     NK_EDIT_SIMPLE  = NK_EDIT_ALWAYS_INSERT_MODE,
   3720     NK_EDIT_FIELD   = NK_EDIT_SIMPLE|NK_EDIT_SELECTABLE|NK_EDIT_CLIPBOARD,
   3721     NK_EDIT_BOX     = NK_EDIT_ALWAYS_INSERT_MODE| NK_EDIT_SELECTABLE| NK_EDIT_MULTILINE|NK_EDIT_ALLOW_TAB|NK_EDIT_CLIPBOARD,
   3722     NK_EDIT_EDITOR  = NK_EDIT_SELECTABLE|NK_EDIT_MULTILINE|NK_EDIT_ALLOW_TAB| NK_EDIT_CLIPBOARD
   3723 };
   3724 enum nk_edit_events {
   3725     NK_EDIT_ACTIVE      = NK_FLAG(0), /**!< edit widget is currently being modified */
   3726     NK_EDIT_INACTIVE    = NK_FLAG(1), /**!< edit widget is not active and is not being modified */
   3727     NK_EDIT_ACTIVATED   = NK_FLAG(2), /**!< edit widget went from state inactive to state active */
   3728     NK_EDIT_DEACTIVATED = NK_FLAG(3), /**!< edit widget went from state active to state inactive */
   3729     NK_EDIT_COMMITED    = NK_FLAG(4)  /**!< edit widget has received an enter and lost focus */
   3730 };

   4062 /**
   4063  * \page Font
   4064  * Font handling in this library was designed to be quite customizable and lets
   4065  * you decide what you want to use and what you want to provide. There are three
   4066  * different ways to use the font atlas. The first two will use your font
   4067  * handling scheme and only requires essential data to run nuklear. The next
   4068  * slightly more advanced features is font handling with vertex buffer output.
   4069  * Finally the most complex API wise is using nuklear's font baking API.
   4070  *
   4071  * # Using your own implementation without vertex buffer output
   4072  *
   4073  * So first up the easiest way to do font handling is by just providing a
   4074  * `nk_user_font` struct which only requires the height in pixel of the used
   4075  * font and a callback to calculate the width of a string. This way of handling
   4076  * fonts is best fitted for using the normal draw shape command API where you
   4077  * do all the text drawing yourself and the library does not require any kind
   4078  * of deeper knowledge about which font handling mechanism you use.
   4079  * IMPORTANT: the `nk_user_font` pointer provided to nuklear has to persist
   4080  * over the complete life time! I know this sucks but it is currently the only
   4081  * way to switch between fonts.
   4082  *
   4083  * ```c
   4084  *     float your_text_width_calculation(nk_handle handle, float height, const char *text, int len)
   4085  *     {
   4086  *         your_font_type *type = handle.ptr;
   4087  *         float text_width = ...;
   4088  *         return text_width;
   4089  *     }
   4090  *
   4091  *     struct nk_user_font font;
   4092  *     font.userdata.ptr = &your_font_class_or_struct;
   4093  *     font.height = your_font_height;
   4094  *     font.width = your_text_width_calculation;
   4095  *
   4096  *     struct nk_context ctx;
   4097  *     nk_init_default(&ctx, &font);
   4098  * ```
   4099  * # Using your own implementation with vertex buffer output
   4100  *
   4101  * While the first approach works fine if you don't want to use the optional
   4102  * vertex buffer output it is not enough if you do. To get font handling working
   4103  * for these cases you have to provide two additional parameters inside the
   4104  * `nk_user_font`. First a texture atlas handle used to draw text as subimages
   4105  * of a bigger font atlas texture and a callback to query a character's glyph
   4106  * information (offset, size, ...). So it is still possible to provide your own
   4107  * font and use the vertex buffer output.
   4108  *
   4109  * ```c
   4110  *     float your_text_width_calculation(nk_handle handle, float height, const char *text, int len)
   4111  *     {
   4112  *         your_font_type *type = handle.ptr;
   4113  *         float text_width = ...;
   4114  *         return text_width;
   4115  *     }
   4116  *     void query_your_font_glyph(nk_handle handle, float font_height, struct nk_user_font_glyph *glyph, nk_rune codepoint, nk_rune next_codepoint)
   4117  *     {
   4118  *         your_font_type *type = handle.ptr;
   4119  *         glyph.width = ...;
   4120  *         glyph.height = ...;
   4121  *         glyph.xadvance = ...;
   4122  *         glyph.uv[0].x = ...;
   4123  *         glyph.uv[0].y = ...;
   4124  *         glyph.uv[1].x = ...;
   4125  *         glyph.uv[1].y = ...;
   4126  *         glyph.offset.x = ...;
   4127  *         glyph.offset.y = ...;
   4128  *     }
   4129  *
   4130  *     struct nk_user_font font;
   4131  *     font.userdata.ptr = &your_font_class_or_struct;
   4132  *     font.height = your_font_height;
   4133  *     font.width = your_text_width_calculation;
   4134  *     font.query = query_your_font_glyph;
   4135  *     font.texture.id = your_font_texture;
   4136  *
   4137  *     struct nk_context ctx;
   4138  *     nk_init_default(&ctx, &font);
   4139  * ```
   4140  *
   4141  * # Nuklear font baker
   4142  *
   4143  * The final approach if you do not have a font handling functionality or don't
   4144  * want to use it in this library is by using the optional font baker.
   4145  * The font baker APIs can be used to create a font plus font atlas texture
   4146  * and can be used with or without the vertex buffer output.
   4147  *
   4148  * It still uses the `nk_user_font` struct and the two different approaches
   4149  * previously stated still work. The font baker is not located inside
   4150  * `nk_context` like all other systems since it can be understood as more of
   4151  * an extension to nuklear and does not really depend on any `nk_context` state.
   4152  *
   4153  * Font baker need to be initialized first by one of the nk_font_atlas_init_xxx
   4154  * functions. If you don't care about memory just call the default version
   4155  * `nk_font_atlas_init_default` which will allocate all memory from the standard library.
   4156  * If you want to control memory allocation but you don't care if the allocated
   4157  * memory is temporary and therefore can be freed directly after the baking process
   4158  * is over or permanent you can call `nk_font_atlas_init`.
   4159  *
   4160  * After successfully initializing the font baker you can add Truetype(.ttf) fonts from
   4161  * different sources like memory or from file by calling one of the `nk_font_atlas_add_xxx`.
   4162  * functions. Adding font will permanently store each font, font config and ttf memory block(!)
   4163  * inside the font atlas and allows to reuse the font atlas. If you don't want to reuse
   4164  * the font baker by for example adding additional fonts you can call
   4165  * `nk_font_atlas_cleanup` after the baking process is over (after calling nk_font_atlas_end).
   4166  *
   4167  * As soon as you added all fonts you wanted you can now start the baking process
   4168  * for every selected glyph to image by calling `nk_font_atlas_bake`.
   4169  * The baking process returns image memory, width and height which can be used to
   4170  * either create your own image object or upload it to any graphics library.
   4171  * No matter which case you finally have to call `nk_font_atlas_end` which
   4172  * will free all temporary memory including the font atlas image so make sure
   4173  * you created our texture beforehand. `nk_font_atlas_end` requires a handle
   4174  * to your font texture or object and optionally fills a `struct nk_draw_null_texture`
   4175  * which can be used for the optional vertex output. If you don't want it just
   4176  * set the argument to `NULL`.
   4177  *
   4178  * At this point you are done and if you don't want to reuse the font atlas you
   4179  * can call `nk_font_atlas_cleanup` to free all truetype blobs and configuration
   4180  * memory. Finally if you don't use the font atlas and any of it's fonts anymore
   4181  * you need to call `nk_font_atlas_clear` to free all memory still being used.
   4182  *
   4183  * ```c
   4184  *     struct nk_font_atlas atlas;
   4185  *     nk_font_atlas_init_default(&atlas);
   4186  *     nk_font_atlas_begin(&atlas);
   4187  *     nk_font *font = nk_font_atlas_add_from_file(&atlas, "Path/To/Your/TTF_Font.ttf", 13, 0);
   4188  *     nk_font *font2 = nk_font_atlas_add_from_file(&atlas, "Path/To/Your/TTF_Font2.ttf", 16, 0);
   4189  *     const void* img = nk_font_atlas_bake(&atlas, &img_width, &img_height, NK_FONT_ATLAS_RGBA32);
   4190  *     nk_font_atlas_end(&atlas, nk_handle_id(texture), 0);
   4191  *
   4192  *     struct nk_context ctx;
   4193  *     nk_init_default(&ctx, &font->handle);
   4194  *     while (1) {
   4195  *
   4196  *     }
   4197  *     nk_font_atlas_clear(&atlas);
   4198  * ```
   4199  * The font baker API is probably the most complex API inside this library and
   4200  * I would suggest reading some of my examples `example/` to get a grip on how
   4201  * to use the font atlas. There are a number of details I left out. For example
   4202  * how to merge fonts, configure a font with `nk_font_config` to use other languages,
   4203  * use another texture coordinate format and a lot more:
   4204  *
   4205  * ```c
   4206  *     struct nk_font_config cfg = nk_font_config(font_pixel_height);
   4207  *     cfg.merge_mode = nk_false or nk_true;
   4208  *     cfg.range = nk_font_korean_glyph_ranges();
   4209  *     cfg.coord_type = NK_COORD_PIXEL;
   4210  *     nk_font *font = nk_font_atlas_add_from_file(&atlas, "Path/To/Your/TTF_Font.ttf", 13, &cfg);
   4211  * ```
   4212  */
   4213

   4350 /** ==============================================================
   4351  *
   4352  *                          MEMORY BUFFER
   4353  *
   4354  * ===============================================================*/
   4355 /**
   4356  * \page Memory Buffer
   4357  * A basic (double)-buffer with linear allocation and resetting as only
   4358  * freeing policy. The buffer's main purpose is to control all memory management
   4359  * inside the GUI toolkit and still leave memory control as much as possible in
   4360  * the hand of the user while also making sure the library is easy to use if
   4361  * not as much control is needed.
   4362  * In general all memory inside this library can be provided from the user in
   4363  * three different ways.
   4364  *
   4365  * The first way and the one providing most control is by just passing a fixed
   4366  * size memory block. In this case all control lies in the hand of the user
   4367  * since he can exactly control where the memory comes from and how much memory
   4368  * the library should consume. Of course using the fixed size API removes the
   4369  * ability to automatically resize a buffer if not enough memory is provided so
   4370  * you have to take over the resizing. While being a fixed sized buffer sounds
   4371  * quite limiting, it is very effective in this library since the actual memory
   4372  * consumption is quite stable and has a fixed upper bound for a lot of cases.
   4373  *
   4374  * If you don't want to think about how much memory the library should allocate
   4375  * at all time or have a very dynamic UI with unpredictable memory consumption
   4376  * habits but still want control over memory allocation you can use the dynamic
   4377  * allocator based API. The allocator consists of two callbacks for allocating
   4378  * and freeing memory and optional userdata so you can plugin your own allocator.
   4379  *
   4380  * The final and easiest way can be used by defining
   4381  * NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOCATOR which uses the standard library memory
   4382  * allocation functions malloc and free and takes over complete control over
   4383  * memory in this library.
   4384  */
   4385 
   4386 struct nk_memory_status {
   4387     void *memory;
   4388     unsigned int type;
   4389     nk_size size;
   4390     nk_size allocated;
   4391     nk_size needed;
   4392     nk_size calls;
   4393 };
   4394 
   4395 enum nk_allocation_type {
   4396     NK_BUFFER_FIXED,
   4397     NK_BUFFER_DYNAMIC
   4398 };
   4399 
   4400 enum nk_buffer_allocation_type {
   4401     NK_BUFFER_FRONT,
   4402     NK_BUFFER_BACK,
   4403     NK_BUFFER_MAX
   4404 };
   4405 
   4406 struct nk_buffer_marker {
   4407     nk_bool active;
   4408     nk_size offset;
   4409 };
   4410 
   4411 struct nk_memory {void *ptr;nk_size size;};
   4412 struct nk_buffer {
   4413     struct nk_buffer_marker marker[NK_BUFFER_MAX]; /**!< buffer marker to free a buffer to a certain offset */
   4414     struct nk_allocator pool;     /**!< allocator callback for dynamic buffers */
   4415     enum nk_allocation_type type; /**!< memory management type */
   4416     struct nk_memory memory;      /**!< memory and size of the current memory block */
   4417     float grow_factor;            /**!< growing factor for dynamic memory management */
   4418     nk_size allocated;            /**!< total amount of memory allocated */
   4419     nk_size needed;               /**!< totally consumed memory given that enough memory is present */
   4420     nk_size calls;                /**!< number of allocation calls */
   4421     nk_size size;                 /**!< current size of the buffer */
   4422 };
   4423 
   4424 #ifdef NK_INCLUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOCATOR
   4425 NK_API void nk_buffer_init_default(struct nk_buffer*);
   4426 #endif
   4427 NK_API void nk_buffer_init(struct nk_buffer*, const struct nk_allocator*, nk_size size);
   4428 NK_API void nk_buffer_init_fixed(struct nk_buffer*, void *memory, nk_size size);
   4429 NK_API void nk_buffer_info(struct nk_memory_status*, const struct nk_buffer*);
   4430 NK_API void nk_buffer_push(struct nk_buffer*, enum nk_buffer_allocation_type type, const void *memory, nk_size size, nk_size align);
   4431 NK_API void nk_buffer_mark(struct nk_buffer*, enum nk_buffer_allocation_type type);
   4432 NK_API void nk_buffer_reset(struct nk_buffer*, enum nk_buffer_allocation_type type);
   4433 NK_API void nk_buffer_clear(struct nk_buffer*);
   4434 NK_API void nk_buffer_free(struct nk_buffer*);
   4435 NK_API void *nk_buffer_memory(struct nk_buffer*);
   4436 NK_API const void *nk_buffer_memory_const(const struct nk_buffer*);
   4437 NK_API nk_size nk_buffer_total(const struct nk_buffer*);

   4495 /**===============================================================
   4496  *
   4497  *                      TEXT EDITOR
   4498  *
   4499  * ===============================================================*/
   4500 /**
   4501  * \page Text Editor
   4502  * Editing text in this library is handled by either `nk_edit_string` or
   4503  * `nk_edit_buffer`. But like almost everything in this library there are multiple
   4504  * ways of doing it and a balance between control and ease of use with memory
   4505  * as well as functionality controlled by flags.
   4506  *
   4507  * This library generally allows three different levels of memory control:
   4508  * First of is the most basic way of just providing a simple char array with
   4509  * string length. This method is probably the easiest way of handling simple
   4510  * user text input. Main upside is complete control over memory while the biggest
   4511  * downside in comparison with the other two approaches is missing undo/redo.
   4512  *
   4513  * For UIs that require undo/redo the second way was created. It is based on
   4514  * a fixed size nk_text_edit struct, which has an internal undo/redo stack.
   4515  * This is mainly useful if you want something more like a text editor but don't want
   4516  * to have a dynamically growing buffer.
   4517  *
   4518  * The final way is using a dynamically growing nk_text_edit struct, which
   4519  * has both a default version if you don't care where memory comes from and an
   4520  * allocator version if you do. While the text editor is quite powerful for its
   4521  * complexity I would not recommend editing gigabytes of data with it.
   4522  * It is rather designed for uses cases which make sense for a GUI library not for
   4523  * an full blown text editor.
   4524  */
   4525 
   4526 #ifndef NK_TEXTEDIT_UNDOSTATECOUNT
   4527 #define NK_TEXTEDIT_UNDOSTATECOUNT     99
   4528 #endif
   4529 
   4530 #ifndef NK_TEXTEDIT_UNDOCHARCOUNT
   4531 #define NK_TEXTEDIT_UNDOCHARCOUNT      999
   4532 #endif
   4533 
   4534 struct nk_text_edit;

   4550    nk_rune undo_char[NK_TEXTEDIT_UNDOCHARCOUNT];
   4551    short undo_point;
   4552    short redo_point;
   4553    short undo_char_point;
   4554    short redo_char_point;
   4555 };

   4613 /* ===============================================================
   4614  *
   4615  *                          DRAWING
   4616  *
   4617  * ===============================================================*/
   4618 /**
   4619  * \page Drawing
   4620  * This library was designed to be render backend agnostic so it does
   4621  * not draw anything to screen. Instead all drawn shapes, widgets
   4622  * are made of, are buffered into memory and make up a command queue.
   4623  * Each frame therefore fills the command buffer with draw commands
   4624  * that then need to be executed by the user and his own render backend.
   4625  * After that the command buffer needs to be cleared and a new frame can be
   4626  * started. It is probably important to note that the command buffer is the main
   4627  * drawing API and the optional vertex buffer API only takes this format and
   4628  * converts it into a hardware accessible format.
   4629  *
   4630  * To use the command queue to draw your own widgets you can access the
   4631  * command buffer of each window by calling `nk_window_get_canvas` after
   4632  * previously having called `nk_begin`:
   4633  *
   4634  * ```c
   4635  *     void draw_red_rectangle_widget(struct nk_context *ctx)
   4636  *     {
   4637  *         struct nk_command_buffer *canvas;
   4638  *         struct nk_input *input = &ctx->input;
   4639  *         canvas = nk_window_get_canvas(ctx);
   4640  *
   4641  *         struct nk_rect space;
   4642  *         enum nk_widget_layout_states state;
   4643  *         state = nk_widget(&space, ctx);
   4644  *         if (!state) return;
   4645  *
   4646  *         if (state != NK_WIDGET_ROM)
   4647  *             update_your_widget_by_user_input(...);
   4648  *         nk_fill_rect(canvas, space, 0, nk_rgb(255,0,0));
   4649  *     }
   4650  *
   4651  *     if (nk_begin(...)) {
   4652  *         nk_layout_row_dynamic(ctx, 25, 1);
   4653  *         draw_red_rectangle_widget(ctx);
   4654  *     }
   4655  *     nk_end(..)
   4656  *
   4657  * ```
   4658  * Important to know if you want to create your own widgets is the `nk_widget`
   4659  * call. It allocates space on the panel reserved for this widget to be used,
   4660  * but also returns the state of the widget space. If your widget is not seen and does
   4661  * not have to be updated it is '0' and you can just return. If it only has
   4662  * to be drawn the state will be `NK_WIDGET_ROM` otherwise you can do both
   4663  * update and draw your widget. The reason for separating is to only draw and
   4664  * update what is actually necessary which is crucial for performance.
   4665  */
   4666 
   4667 enum nk_command_type {
   4668     NK_COMMAND_NOP,
   4669     NK_COMMAND_SCISSOR,
   4670     NK_COMMAND_LINE,
   4671     NK_COMMAND_CURVE,
   4672     NK_COMMAND_RECT,
   4673     NK_COMMAND_RECT_FILLED,
   4674     NK_COMMAND_RECT_MULTI_COLOR,
   4675     NK_COMMAND_CIRCLE,
   4676     NK_COMMAND_CIRCLE_FILLED,
   4677     NK_COMMAND_ARC,
   4678     NK_COMMAND_ARC_FILLED,
   4679     NK_COMMAND_TRIANGLE,
   4680     NK_COMMAND_TRIANGLE_FILLED,
   4681     NK_COMMAND_POLYGON,
   4682     NK_COMMAND_POLYGON_FILLED,
   4683     NK_COMMAND_POLYLINE,
   4684     NK_COMMAND_TEXT,
   4685     NK_COMMAND_IMAGE,
   4686     NK_COMMAND_CUSTOM
   4687 };
   4688

   4944 /* ===============================================================
   4945  *
   4946  *                          DRAW LIST
   4947  *
   4948  * ===============================================================*/
   4949 #ifdef NK_INCLUDE_VERTEX_BUFFER_OUTPUT
   4950 /**
   4951  * \page "Draw List"
   4952  * The optional vertex buffer draw list provides a 2D drawing context
   4953  * with antialiasing functionality which takes basic filled or outlined shapes
   4954  * or a path and outputs vertexes, elements and draw commands.
   4955  * The actual draw list API is not required to be used directly while using this
   4956  * library since converting the default library draw command output is done by
   4957  * just calling `nk_convert` but I decided to still make this library accessible
   4958  * since it can be useful.
   4959  *
   4960  * The draw list is based on a path buffering and polygon and polyline
   4961  * rendering API which allows a lot of ways to draw 2D content to screen.
   4962  * In fact it is probably more powerful than needed but allows even more crazy
   4963  * things than this library provides by default.
   4964  */
   4965 
   4966 #ifdef NK_UINT_DRAW_INDEX
   4967 typedef nk_uint nk_draw_index;
   4968 #else
   4969 typedef nk_ushort nk_draw_index;
   4970 #endif
   4971 enum nk_draw_list_stroke {
   4972     NK_STROKE_OPEN = nk_false, /***< build up path has no connection back to the beginning */
   4973     NK_STROKE_CLOSED = nk_true /***< build up path has a connection back to the beginning */
   4974 };
   4975 
   4976 enum nk_draw_vertex_layout_attribute {
   4977     NK_VERTEX_POSITION,
   4978     NK_VERTEX_COLOR,
   4979     NK_VERTEX_TEXCOORD,
   4980     NK_VERTEX_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT
   4981 };
   4982 
   4983 enum nk_draw_vertex_layout_format {
   4984     NK_FORMAT_SCHAR,
   4985     NK_FORMAT_SSHORT,
   4986     NK_FORMAT_SINT,
   4987     NK_FORMAT_UCHAR,
   4988     NK_FORMAT_USHORT,
   4989     NK_FORMAT_UINT,
   4990     NK_FORMAT_FLOAT,
   4991     NK_FORMAT_DOUBLE,
   4992 
   4993 NK_FORMAT_COLOR_BEGIN,
   4994     NK_FORMAT_R8G8B8 = NK_FORMAT_COLOR_BEGIN,
   4995     NK_FORMAT_R16G15B16,
   4996     NK_FORMAT_R32G32B32,
   4997

   5789 /*==============================================================
   5790  *                          STACK
   5791  * =============================================================*/
   5792 /**
   5793  * \page Stack
   5794  * # Stack
   5795  * The style modifier stack can be used to temporarily change a
   5796  * property inside `nk_style`. For example if you want a special
   5797  * red button you can temporarily push the old button color onto a stack
   5798  * draw the button with a red color and then you just pop the old color
   5799  * back from the stack:
   5800  *
   5801  *     nk_style_push_style_item(ctx, &ctx->style.button.normal, nk_style_item_color(nk_rgb(255,0,0)));
   5802  *     nk_style_push_style_item(ctx, &ctx->style.button.hover, nk_style_item_color(nk_rgb(255,0,0)));
   5803  *     nk_style_push_style_item(ctx, &ctx->style.button.active, nk_style_item_color(nk_rgb(255,0,0)));
   5804  *     nk_style_push_vec2(ctx, &cx->style.button.padding, nk_vec2(2,2));
   5805  *
   5806  *     nk_button(...);
   5807  *
   5808  *     nk_style_pop_style_item(ctx);
   5809  *     nk_style_pop_style_item(ctx);
   5810  *     nk_style_pop_style_item(ctx);
   5811  *     nk_style_pop_vec2(ctx);
   5812  *
   5813  * Nuklear has a stack for style_items, float properties, vector properties,
   5814  * flags, colors, fonts and for button_behavior. Each has it's own fixed size stack
   5815  * which can be changed at compile time.
   5816  */
   5817 
   5818 #ifndef NK_BUTTON_BEHAVIOR_STACK_SIZE
   5819 #define NK_BUTTON_BEHAVIOR_STACK_SIZE 8
   5820 #endif
   5821 
   5822 #ifndef NK_FONT_STACK_SIZE
   5823 #define NK_FONT_STACK_SIZE 8
   5824 #endif
   5825 
   5826 #ifndef NK_STYLE_ITEM_STACK_SIZE
   5827 #define NK_STYLE_ITEM_STACK_SIZE 16
   5828 #endif
   5829 
   5830 #ifndef NK_FLOAT_STACK_SIZE
   5831 #define NK_FLOAT_STACK_SIZE 32
   5832 #endif
   5833 
   5834 #ifndef NK_VECTOR_STACK_SIZE
   5835 #define NK_VECTOR_STACK_SIZE 16
   5836 #endif
   5837 
   5838 #ifndef NK_FLAGS_STACK_SIZE
   5839 #define NK_FLAGS_STACK_SIZE 32
   5840 #endif
   5841 
   5842 #ifndef NK_COLOR_STACK_SIZE
   5843 #define NK_COLOR_STACK_SIZE 32
   5844 #endif
   5845 
   5846 #define NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(prefix, name, type)\
   5847     struct nk_config_stack_##name##_element {\
   5848         prefix##_##type *address;\
   5849         prefix##_##type old_value;\
   5850     }
   5851 #define NK_CONFIG_STACK(type,size)\
   5852     struct nk_config_stack_##type {\
   5853         int head;\
   5854         struct nk_config_stack_##type##_element elements[size];\
   5855     }
   5856 
   5857 #define nk_float float
   5858 NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(struct nk, style_item, style_item);
   5859 NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(nk ,float, float);
   5860 NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(struct nk, vec2, vec2);
   5861 NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(nk ,flags, flags);
   5862 NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(struct nk, color, color);
   5863 NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(const struct nk, user_font, user_font*);
   5864 NK_CONFIGURATION_STACK_TYPE(enum nk, button_behavior, button_behavior);
   5865 
   5866 NK_CONFIG_STACK(style_item, NK_STYLE_ITEM_STACK_SIZE);
   5867 NK_CONFIG_STACK(float, NK_FLOAT_STACK_SIZE);
   5868 NK_CONFIG_STACK(vec2, NK_VECTOR_STACK_SIZE);
   5869 NK_CONFIG_STACK(flags, NK_FLAGS_STACK_SIZE);
   5870 NK_CONFIG_STACK(color, NK_COLOR_STACK_SIZE);
   5871 NK_CONFIG_STACK(user_font, NK_FONT_STACK_SIZE);
   5872 NK_CONFIG_STACK(button_behavior, NK_BUTTON_BEHAVIOR_STACK_SIZE);
   5873

   5971 #define NK_PI 3.141592654f
   5972 #define NK_PI_HALF 1.570796326f
   5973 #define NK_UTF_INVALID 0xFFFD
   5974 #define NK_MAX_FLOAT_PRECISION 2
   5975 
   5976 #define NK_UNUSED(x) ((void)(x))
   5977 #define NK_SATURATE(x) (NK_MAX(0, NK_MIN(1.0f, x)))
   5978 #define NK_LEN(a) (sizeof(a)/sizeof(a)[0])
   5979 #define NK_ABS(a) (((a) < 0) ? -(a) : (a))
   5980 #define NK_BETWEEN(x, a, b) ((a) <= (x) && (x) < (b))
   5981 #define NK_INBOX(px, py, x, y, w, h)\
   5982     (NK_BETWEEN(px,x,x+w) && NK_BETWEEN(py,y,y+h))
   5983 #define NK_INTERSECT(x0, y0, w0, h0, x1, y1, w1, h1) \
   5984     ((x1 < (x0 + w0)) && (x0 < (x1 + w1)) && \
   5985     (y1 < (y0 + h0)) && (y0 < (y1 + h1)))
   5986 #define NK_CONTAINS(x, y, w, h, bx, by, bw, bh)\
   5987     (NK_INBOX(x,y, bx, by, bw, bh) && NK_INBOX(x+w,y+h, bx, by, bw, bh))
   5988 
   5989 #define nk_vec2_sub(a, b) nk_vec2((a).x - (b).x, (a).y - (b).y)
   5990 #define nk_vec2_add(a, b) nk_vec2((a).x + (b).x, (a).y + (b).y)
   5991 #define nk_vec2_len_sqr(a) ((a).x*(a).x+(a).y*(a).y)
   5992 #define nk_vec2_muls(a, t) nk_vec2((a).x * (t), (a).y * (t))
   5993 
   5994 #define nk_ptr_add(t, p, i) ((t*)((void*)((nk_byte*)(p) + (i))))
   5995 #define nk_ptr_add_const(t, p, i) ((const t*)((const void*)((const nk_byte*)(p) + (i))))
   5996 #define nk_zero_struct(s) nk_zero(&s, sizeof(s))

   5998 /* ==============================================================
   5999  *                          ALIGNMENT
   6000  * =============================================================== */
   6001 /* Pointer to Integer type conversion for pointer alignment */
   6002 #if defined(__PTRDIFF_TYPE__) /* This case should work for GCC*/
   6003 # define NK_UINT_TO_PTR(x) ((void*)(__PTRDIFF_TYPE__)(x))
   6004 # define NK_PTR_TO_UINT(x) ((nk_size)(__PTRDIFF_TYPE__)(x))
   6005 #elif !defined(__GNUC__) /* works for compilers other than LLVM */
   6006 # define NK_UINT_TO_PTR(x) ((void*)&((char*)0)[x])
   6007 # define NK_PTR_TO_UINT(x) ((nk_size)(((char*)x)-(char*)0))
   6008 #elif defined(NK_USE_FIXED_TYPES) /* used if we have <stdint.h> */
   6009 # define NK_UINT_TO_PTR(x) ((void*)(uintptr_t)(x))
   6010 # define NK_PTR_TO_UINT(x) ((uintptr_t)(x))
   6011 #else /* generates warning but works */
   6012 # define NK_UINT_TO_PTR(x) ((void*)(x))
   6013 # define NK_PTR_TO_UINT(x) ((nk_size)(x))
   6014 #endif
   6015 
   6016 #define NK_ALIGN_PTR(x, mask)\
   6017     (NK_UINT_TO_PTR((NK_PTR_TO_UINT((nk_byte*)(x) + (mask-1)) & ~(mask-1))))
   6018 #define NK_ALIGN_PTR_BACK(x, mask)\
   6019     (NK_UINT_TO_PTR((NK_PTR_TO_UINT((nk_byte*)(x)) & ~(mask-1))))
   6020 
   6021 #if ((defined(__GNUC__) && __GNUC__ >= 4) || defined(__clang__)) && !defined(EMSCRIPTEN)
   6022 #define NK_OFFSETOF(st,m) (__builtin_offsetof(st,m))
   6023 #else
   6024 #define NK_OFFSETOF(st,m) ((nk_ptr)&(((st*)0)->m))
   6025 #endif
   6026 
   6027 #ifdef __cplusplus
   6028 }
   6029 #endif
   6030 
   6031 #ifdef __cplusplus
   6032 template<typename T> struct nk_alignof;
   6033 template<typename T, int size_diff> struct nk_helper{enum {value = size_diff};};
   6034 template<typename T> struct nk_helper<T,0>{enum {value = nk_alignof<T>::value};};
   6035 template<typename T> struct nk_alignof{struct Big {T x; char c;}; enum {
   6036     diff = sizeof(Big) - sizeof(T), value = nk_helper<Big, diff>::value};};
   6037 #define NK_ALIGNOF(t) (nk_alignof<t>::value)
   6038 #else
   6039 #define NK_ALIGNOF(t) NK_OFFSETOF(struct {char c; t _h;}, _h)
   6040 #endif
   6041 
   6042 #define NK_CONTAINER_OF(ptr,type,member)\
   6043     (type*)((void*)((char*)(1 ? (ptr): &((type*)0)->member) - NK_OFFSETOF(type, member)))

   6432 /* ===============================================================
   6433  *
   6434  *                              MATH
   6435  *
   6436  * ===============================================================*/
   6437 /*/// ### Math
   6438 ///  Since nuklear is supposed to work on all systems providing floating point
   6439 ///  math without any dependencies I also had to implement my own math functions
   6440 ///  for sqrt, sin and cos. Since the actual highly accurate implementations for
   6441 ///  the standard library functions are quite complex and I do not need high
   6442 ///  precision for my use cases I use approximations.
   6443 ///
   6444 ///  Sqrt
   6445 ///  ----
   6446 ///  For square root nuklear uses the famous fast inverse square root:
   6447 ///  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_inverse_square_root with
   6448 ///  slightly tweaked magic constant. While on today's hardware it is
   6449 ///  probably not faster it is still fast and accurate enough for
   6450 ///  nuklear's use cases. IMPORTANT: this requires float format IEEE 754
   6451 ///
   6452 ///  Sine/Cosine
   6453 ///  -----------
   6454 ///  All constants inside both function are generated Remez's minimax
   6455 ///  approximations for value range 0...2*PI. The reason why I decided to
   6456 ///  approximate exactly that range is that nuklear only needs sine and
   6457 ///  cosine to generate circles which only requires that exact range.
   6458 ///  In addition I used Remez instead of Taylor for additional precision:
   6459 ///  www.lolengine.net/blog/2011/12/21/better-function-approximations.
   6460 ///
   6461 ///  The tool I used to generate constants for both sine and cosine
   6462 ///  (it can actually approximate a lot more functions) can be
   6463 ///  found here: www.lolengine.net/wiki/oss/lolremez
   6464 */
   6465 #ifndef NK_INV_SQRT
   6466 #define NK_INV_SQRT nk_inv_sqrt
   6467 NK_LIB float
   6468 nk_inv_sqrt(float n)
   6469 {
   6470     float x2;
   6471     const float threehalfs = 1.5f;
   6472     union {nk_uint i; float f;} conv = {0};
   6473     conv.f = n;
   6474     x2 = n * 0.5f;
   6475     conv.i = 0x5f375A84 - (conv.i >> 1);
   6476     conv.f = conv.f * (threehalfs - (x2 * conv.f * conv.f));
   6477     return conv.f;
   6478 }
   6479 #endif
   6480 #ifndef NK_SIN
   6481 #define NK_SIN nk_sin
   6482 NK_LIB float
   6483 nk_sin(float x)
   6484 {
   6485     NK_STORAGE const float a0 = +1.91059300966915117e-31f;
   6486     NK_STORAGE const float a1 = +1.00086760103908896f;
   6487     NK_STORAGE const float a2 = -1.21276126894734565e-2f;
   6488     NK_STORAGE const float a3 = -1.38078780785773762e-1f;
   6489     NK_STORAGE const float a4 = -2.67353392911981221e-2f;
   6490     NK_STORAGE const float a5 = +2.08026600266304389e-2f;
   6491     NK_STORAGE const float a6 = -3.03996055049204407e-3f;
   6492     NK_STORAGE const float a7 = +1.38235642404333740e-4f;
   6493     return a0 + x*(a1 + x*(a2 + x*(a3 + x*(a4 + x*(a5 + x*(a6 + x*a7))))));
   6494 }
   6495 #endif
   6496 #ifndef NK_COS
   6497 #define NK_COS nk_cos
   6498 NK_LIB float
   6499 nk_cos(float x)
   6500 {
   6501     /* New implementation. Also generated using lolremez. */
   6502     /* Old version significantly deviated from expected results. */
   6503     NK_STORAGE const float a0 = 9.9995999154986614e-1f;
   6504     NK_STORAGE const float a1 = 1.2548995793001028e-3f;
   6505     NK_STORAGE const float a2 = -5.0648546280678015e-1f;
   6506     NK_STORAGE const float a3 = 1.2942246466519995e-2f;
   6507     NK_STORAGE const float a4 = 2.8668384702547972e-2f;
   6508     NK_STORAGE const float a5 = 7.3726485210586547e-3f;
   6509     NK_STORAGE const float a6 = -3.8510875386947414e-3f;
   6510     NK_STORAGE const float a7 = 4.7196604604366623e-4f;
   6511     NK_STORAGE const float a8 = -1.8776444013090451e-5f;
   6512     return a0 + x*(a1 + x*(a2 + x*(a3 + x*(a4 + x*(a5 + x*(a6 + x*(a7 + x*a8)))))));
   6513 }
   6514 #endif
   6515 #ifndef NK_ATAN
   6516 #define NK_ATAN nk_atan
   6517 NK_LIB float
   6518 nk_atan(float x)
   6519 {
   6520     /* ./lolremez --progress --float -d 9 -r "0:pi*2" "atan(x)" */
   6521     float u = -1.0989005e-05f;
   6522     NK_ASSERT(x >= 0.0f && "TODO support negative floats");
   6523     u = u * x + 0.00034117949f;
   6524     u = u * x + -0.0044932296f;
   6525     u = u * x + 0.032596264f;
   6526     u = u * x + -0.14088021f;
   6527     u = u * x + 0.36040401f;
   6528     u = u * x + -0.47017866f;
   6529     u = u * x + 0.00050198776f;
   6530     u = u * x + 1.0077682f;
   6531     u = u * x + -0.0004765437f;
   6532     return u;
   6533 }
   6534 #endif
   6535 #ifndef NK_ATAN2
   6536 #define NK_ATAN2 nk_atan2
   6537 NK_LIB float
   6538 nk_atan2(float y, float x)
   6539 {
   6540     float ax = NK_ABS(x),
   6541           ay = NK_ABS(y);
   6542     /* 0 = +y +x    1 = -y +x
   6543        2 = +y -x    3 = -y -x */
   6544     nk_uint signs = (y < 0) | ((x < 0) << 1);
   6545 
   6546     float a;
   6547     if(y == 0.0 && x == 0.0) return 0.0f;
   6548     a = (ay > ax)
   6549         ? NK_PI_HALF - NK_ATAN(ax / ay)
   6550         : NK_ATAN(ay / ax);
   6551 
   6552     switch(signs){
   6553         case 0: return a;
   6554         case 1: return -a;
   6555         case 2: return -a + NK_PI;
   6556         case 3: return a - NK_PI;
   6557     }
   6558     return 0.0f; /* prevents warning */
   6559 }
   6560 #endif
   6561 NK_LIB nk_uint
   6562 nk_round_up_pow2(nk_uint v)
   6563 {
   6564     v--;
   6565     v |= v >> 1;
   6566     v |= v >> 2;
   6567     v |= v >> 4;
   6568     v |= v >> 8;
   6569     v |= v >> 16;
   6570     v++;
   6571     return v;
   6572 }
   6573 NK_LIB double
   6574 nk_pow(double x, int n)
   6575 {
   6576     /*  check the sign of n */
   6577     double r = 1;
   6578     int plus = n >= 0;
   6579     n = (plus) ? n : -n;
   6580     while (n > 0) {
   6581         if ((n & 1) == 1)
   6582             r *= x;
   6583         n /= 2;
   6584         x *= x;
   6585     }
   6586     return plus ? r : 1.0 / r;
   6587 }
   6588 NK_LIB int
   6589 nk_ifloord(double x)
   6590 {
   6591     x = (double)((int)x - ((x < 0.0) ? 1 : 0));
   6592     return (int)x;
   6593 }
   6594 NK_LIB int
   6595 nk_ifloorf(float x)
   6596 {
   6597     x = (float)((int)x - ((x < 0.0f) ? 1 : 0));
   6598     return (int)x;
   6599 }
   6600 NK_LIB int
   6601 nk_iceilf(float x)
   6602 {
   6603     if (x >= 0) {
   6604         int i = (int)x;
   6605         return (x > i) ? i+1: i;
   6606     } else {
   6607         int t = (int)x;
   6608         float r = x - (float)t;
   6609         return (r > 0.0f) ? t+1: t;
   6610     }
   6611 }
   6612 NK_LIB int
   6613 nk_log10(double n)
   6614 {
   6615     int neg;
   6616     int ret;
   6617     int exp = 0;
   6618 
   6619     neg = (n < 0) ? 1 : 0;
   6620     ret = (neg) ? (int)-n : (int)n;
   6621     while ((ret / 10) > 0) {
   6622         ret /= 10;
   6623         exp++;
   6624     }
   6625     if (neg) exp = -exp;
   6626     return exp;
   6627 }
   6628 NK_LIB float
   6629 nk_roundf(float x)
   6630 {
   6631     return (x >= 0.0f) ? (float)nk_ifloorf(x + 0.5f) : (float)nk_iceilf(x - 0.5f);
   6632 }

   6685 NK_LIB struct nk_rect
   6686 nk_shrink_rect(struct nk_rect r, float amount)
   6687 {
   6688     struct nk_rect res;
   6689     r.w = NK_MAX(r.w, 2 * amount);
   6690     r.h = NK_MAX(r.h, 2 * amount);
   6691     res.x = r.x + amount;
   6692     res.y = r.y + amount;
   6693     res.w = r.w - 2 * amount;
   6694     res.h = r.h - 2 * amount;
   6695     return res;
   6696 }
   6697 NK_LIB struct nk_rect
   6698 nk_pad_rect(struct nk_rect r, struct nk_vec2 pad)
   6699 {
   6700     r.w = NK_MAX(r.w, 2 * pad.x);
   6701     r.h = NK_MAX(r.h, 2 * pad.y);
   6702     r.x += pad.x; r.y += pad.y;
   6703     r.w -= 2 * pad.x;
   6704     r.h -= 2 * pad.y;
   6705     return r;
   6706 }

   6732 NK_LIB void
   6733 nk_unify(struct nk_rect *clip, const struct nk_rect *a, float x0, float y0,
   6734     float x1, float y1)
   6735 {
   6736     NK_ASSERT(a);
   6737     NK_ASSERT(clip);
   6738     clip->x = NK_MAX(a->x, x0);
   6739     clip->y = NK_MAX(a->y, y0);
   6740     clip->w = NK_MIN(a->x + a->w, x1) - clip->x;
   6741     clip->h = NK_MIN(a->y + a->h, y1) - clip->y;
   6742     clip->w = NK_MAX(0, clip->w);
   6743     clip->h = NK_MAX(0, clip->h);
   6744 }

   6746 NK_API void
   6747 nk_triangle_from_direction(struct nk_vec2 *result, struct nk_rect r,
   6748     float pad_x, float pad_y, enum nk_heading direction)
   6749 {
   6750     float w_half, h_half;
   6751     NK_ASSERT(result);
   6752 
   6753     r.w = NK_MAX(2 * pad_x, r.w);
   6754     r.h = NK_MAX(2 * pad_y, r.h);
   6755     r.w = r.w - 2 * pad_x;
   6756     r.h = r.h - 2 * pad_y;
   6757 
   6758     r.x = r.x + pad_x;
   6759     r.y = r.y + pad_y;
   6760 
   6761     w_half = r.w / 2.0f;
   6762     h_half = r.h / 2.0f;
   6763 
   6764     if (direction == NK_UP) {
   6765         result[0] = nk_vec2(r.x + w_half, r.y);
   6766         result[1] = nk_vec2(r.x + r.w, r.y + r.h);
   6767         result[2] = nk_vec2(r.x, r.y + r.h);
   6768     } else if (direction == NK_RIGHT) {
   6769         result[0] = nk_vec2(r.x, r.y);
   6770         result[1] = nk_vec2(r.x + r.w, r.y + h_half);
   6771         result[2] = nk_vec2(r.x, r.y + r.h);
   6772     } else if (direction == NK_DOWN) {
   6773         result[0] = nk_vec2(r.x, r.y);
   6774         result[1] = nk_vec2(r.x + r.w, r.y);
   6775         result[2] = nk_vec2(r.x + w_half, r.y + r.h);
   6776     } else {
   6777         result[0] = nk_vec2(r.x, r.y + h_half);
   6778         result[1] = nk_vec2(r.x + r.w, r.y);
   6779         result[2] = nk_vec2(r.x + r.w, r.y + r.h);
   6780     }
   6781 }

   6794 NK_LIB nk_bool nk_is_lower(int c) {return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 0xE0 && c <= 0xFF);}
   6795 NK_LIB nk_bool nk_is_upper(int c){return (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 0xC0 && c <= 0xDF);}
   6796 NK_LIB int nk_to_upper(int c) {return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') ? (c - ('a' - 'A')) : c;}
   6797 NK_LIB int nk_to_lower(int c) {return (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') ? (c - ('a' + 'A')) : c;}
